title: Re-directing and re-distributing Lichtenberg discharges—A new type of injection barrier on dielectrics
abstract: Georg Christoph Lichtenberg’s 1777 seminal discovery of fractal electric-discharge patterns (Lichtenberg figures) and later findings of related fulgurites are briefly recounted. Inspired by these, University of Connecticut researchers created ordered montmorillonite nano-coatings that form a barrier and redirect carriers in-plane, effectively protecting insulation materials from intense charge injection and electric discharge.

title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
abstract: Additive-mediated orientation of Zn electrocrystallization is generally attributed to selective facet adsorption of the additives, yet this conventional wisdom is increasingly challenged by mounting literature counterexamples. Here we unravel the relationship between oriented Zn electrocrystallization and the atomic-scale physical variations of different Zn facets upon additive adsorption through extensive case-by-case experimental and computational investigations covering 29 additives. We confirm that the variation of work function upon facet-dependent additive adsorption is the governing factor for crystallographic orientation, achieving a prediction accuracy of 93.1%. This finding suggests a fundamental criterion for additive screening towards favourably oriented Zn electrocrystallization. In addition, further electrochemical investigations reveal that Zn electrocrystallization featuring preferred (100) orientation delivers outstanding cyclability even under harsh conditions of high current density (up to 20 mA cm-2) and deep cycling (depth of discharge >85%), which challenges the consensus that the (002) is the optimal orientation for practical Zn anodes.

title: Molecule-to-System Design Rules for Neutral TEMPO/Viologen Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: Neutral-pH aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) based on TEMPO catholytes and viologen anolytes have emerged as one of the most intensively developed molecular pairings for safe, scalable, long-duration energy...

title: A nonlinear superinductor in a deep-submicrometre integrated circuit
abstract: Superinductors are circuit elements characterized by an intrinsic impedance in excess of the superconducting resistance quantum (RQ ≈ 6.45 kΩ) and are of use in metrology, sensing and quantum computing. However, they are typically based on bespoke structures with high density inductance such as Josephson junctions, superconducting nanowires or twisted two-dimensional materials. Here we report a superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process (GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process). The superinductor leverages the high kinetic inductance (around 1 nH sq−1) of titanium nitride thin films native to the manufacturing process. By co-integrating a resonator containing the superinductor and a silicon quantum dot formed within the same integrated circuit, we create a radio-frequency single-electron transistor, which is widely used as a sensor in semiconductor-based quantum computers. Our sensor has a small footprint of 18 μm2, and offers low parasitics, which, together with the high impedance and nonlinear response of the resonator, yields a power signal-to-noise ratio of 4,500 in an integration time of 4 ns. Our approach could lead to the development of parametric circuits, kinetic-inductance detectors and quantum simulators based on one-dimensional and two-dimensional resonator arrays using integrated circuits. A superinductor can be created in a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process and used to build a radio-frequency single-electron transistor with a compact footprint and high sensitivity.

title: Cross-scale observations of expanding bifurcated current sheets in fast magnetic reconnection
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a universal process that rapidly releases magnetic energy in plasmas, driving explosive phenomena in both space and laboratory environments. Yet a complete understanding of how reconnection proceeds in large-scale plasmas remains elusive. Here we show that expanding bifurcated current sheets (EBCS) are a recurring structure of quasi-steady reconnection. EBCS are double-peaked current layers that expand along the boundaries of the reconnection outflow, accompanied by localized electric fields and strong ion acceleration. We identify this structure consistently in laboratory experiments, spacecraft observations near Earth and the Sun, and large-scale kinetic simulations. Our results indicate that EBCS arise from two-fluid plasma dynamics and occur during quasi-steady antiparallel reconnection, particularly for plasmas with moderate plasma beta (0.1 β ≲ 1, where β is the ratio of plasma thermal pressure to magnetic pressure). These findings link laboratory and space observations to the classical Petschek model and show how two-fluid dynamics can produce open reconnection outflows across widely different system sizes.

title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI.

title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here we report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a Pd/Cu co-catalyzed process. By embedding a carbene insertion step into the Suzuki–Miyaura manifold and overcoming the longstanding chemoselectivity challenge between carbene insertion and direct cross-coupling, this strategy enables the construction of two C–C bonds at a central methine and grants access to three-dimensional chemical space with broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. DFT studies indicate that the Cu co-catalyst governs the relative timing of transmetalation versus carbene insertion at two key junctures in the Pd catalytic cycle, thereby enforcing the desired reaction order. The utility of this method is demonstrated through streamlined syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and analogues, alongside diverse downstream derivatizations.

title: Nanoscopic cation heterogeneity dictates the ambient stability of halide perovskites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ambient instability in formamidinium-caesium mixed-cation perovskites limits the efficiency and long-term durability of solar cells, yet its nanoscopic origin remains unclear. Using quasi-in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify Cs-enriched grain triple junctions as intrinsic weak points under ambient exposure, where Cs⁺ segregation and phase separation initiate. This localized instability induces structural disordering and δ-CsPbI3 crystallization, which propagates into neighboring grains, progressively degrading the perovskite matrix and interfacial optoelectronic properties. To suppress cation heterogeneity, we introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes homogeneous cation distribution, and passivates grain boundaries, thereby enhancing resistance to water and oxygen intrusion. The resulting n-i-p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.37% and retain 96.47% of initial performance after 2,200 h under ISOS-L-1l protocol. Our findings elucidate the nanoscopic ambient degradation pathways in FA-Cs perovskites, establishing a promising strategy for achieving robust perovskite photovoltaics combining high efficiency with long-term durability.

title: Bell nonlocality with directly generated telecom-band spin–photon entanglement
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantum nonlocality, typically revealed through entanglement distribution across quantum networks, is a cornerstone of quantum information science. Long-distance distribution of entanglement requires the information carrier, i.e., flying photons, to operate in the minimum-loss telecom band of optical fiber. While extensive efforts have been devoted to the direct generation of entanglement between C-band telecom photons and various stationary spins, the verification of quantum nonlocality remains an outstanding challenge. Here, utilizing a dipole transition in rubidium atoms with a wavelength of 1530 nm and a cavity-assisted protocol, we achieve resonant excitation and direct emission of C-band telecom photons from a single atom, generating spin–photon entanglement with a measured Bell state fidelity exceeding 91.4%. We then verify Bell nonlocality by observing a Bell inequality violation of 2.455(77) > 2 using this high-quality entangled pair. These results extend the wavelength of a single-atom quantum emitter to the telecom C-band, achieving sufficiently high-fidelity spin–photon entanglement to finally verify Bell nonlocality.

title: Driving catalysts to the intrinsic optical selectivity limit for accelerating photothermal catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Optimizing the photothermal conversion (maximized solar absorption, minimized mid-infrared emissivity) and catalytic activity is essential for constructing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. However, most catalysts lack intrinsic optical selectivity (i.e., high αsolar and low εMIR) and fail to suppress εMIR, which significantly compromises their catalytic performance. Herein, we propose an optical depth strategy to drive catalysts to their intrinsic optical selectivity limit. Demonstrated in metal oxides, this approach simultaneously maximizes αsolar and minimizes εMIR without compromising intrinsic catalytic activity. Demonstrated in the photothermal Sabatier and Bosch processes, our strategy increases methane production by ~590% and carbon nanotube yield by ~200%. Notably, the optimized Co2.85Ru0.15O4 optically selective catalyst exhibits a ~ 26.7% increase in photothermal conversion efficiency. This enhancement leads to a record CH4 production rate of 3375.5 mmol gcat−1 h−1 at a light intensity of 2.8 W cm−2. This innovative strategy highlights the prospects for achieving intrinsic optical selectivity in photothermal catalysts.

title: A sublattice polarimeter to probe the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Measuring the electronic structure of crystalline materials is key in advancing our understanding of their physical properties. While techniques such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy have provided unprecedented insights into electronic orbitals of natural crystals, an equivalent tool to characterize photonic lattices is still lacking. Here, we introduce a sublattice polarimeter that enables full reconstruction of the Bloch wavefunctions in bipartite photonic lattices. Using a spatial light modulator to apply controlled phase shifts and attenuations to each sublattice, we extract the amplitude and phase of the crystal orbitals across the Brillouin zone, including close to band degeneracies. This allows experimentally accessing the Bloch Hamiltonian, thereby determining the quantum geometric tensor and the band Chern numbers. Beyond bipartite lattices, the method can be generalized to address multiple internal degrees of freedom, opening routes to experimentally probe complex topological structures such as trigonal warping, Chern insulators and Euler curvature in multiband settings.

title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga3+ for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ammonia is a promising hydrogen carrier for producing COx-free hydrogen. However, its decomposition suffers from high reaction temperatures. This study reveals that trace Ga doping markedly boosts the low-temperature activity of Ni/Al2O3 catalyst for ammonia decomposition. The Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst achieves 92.0% ammonia conversion at 500 oC and weight hourly space velocity (WHSV) = 30,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic experiments demonstrate that the introduction of Ga species alleviates catalyst hydrogen poisoning. Further studies confirm that Ga preferentially segregates on the catalyst surface and disperses around Ni nanoparticles. Interfacial Ga species facilitate hydrogen spillover from Ni to the Al2O3 support, which promotes the enrichment of adsorbed N* species and reduces their recombination temperature on the Ni surface. This work develops an efficient and stable Ni-based catalyst for low-temperature ammonia decomposition and provides a strategy for optimizing catalytic performance via the regulation of interfacial hydrogen transfer.

title: Quantized even number of vortices in a confined PTO/STO ferroelectric heterostructure with edge pinning effect
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures exhibit rich physical phenomena, but controlling their number and stability remains challenging. We investigate polar vortices in laterally confined lead titanate slabs embedded in a strontium titanate matrix on a dysprosium scandate substrate. Phase-field simulations and transmission electron microscopy show that lateral confinement favors discrete, even numbers of vortices. Energy analysis attributes this preference to competition among Landau, elastic, electrostatic and gradient contributions. Simulations and in situ electrical biasing observations further reveal that polar vortices near slab edges remain stable while interior regions switch under applied field, and vortex configurations recover after the applied voltage is removed. Here, we show that lateral confinement and edge pinning provide a route to controlling the number and switching behavior of polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures.

title: Three-dimensional assessment of toroidal heat-load distribution on divertor targets in EAST
abstract: Although actively cooled W/Cu monoblock targets are designed for high steady-state heat exhaust, local overheating and damage have been observed on these targets in EAST. These observations suggest that, beyond the nominal heat-removal capability, the practical thermal margin may be compromised by engineering alignment, target geometry and plasma operating conditions—all of which can alter the local surface-normal heat flux via modifications in magnetic incidence and magnetic shadowing. In this work, the toroidal distribution of the heat loads on the EAST divertor is analyzed by integrating infrared thermography, finite element heat flux inversion, and three-dimensional field-line tracing using PFCFlux. This analysis focuses on the effects of toroidal-field ripple, cassette misalignment in the presence of ripple, and divertor geometry. It is shown that the 16-fold toroidal field ripple can produce a modulation of the peak heat flux on the current upper outer divertor target, with a peak fluctuation amplitude of approximately . Under a peak heat flux constraint of , the allowable average heat flux on the upper outer target (OT) decreases from in the absence of ripple to in the presence of ripple. When ripple and relative cassette misalignments are considered simultaneously for the same target, the allowable average heat flux is further reduced to 3.11 , 2.79 , and for = 0.6 , 1.0 , and , respectively. Compared with the present upper OT, the toroidally curved lower outer vertical target (OVT) has higher allowable average heat fluxes under both ripple-free and ripple conditions without cassette misalignment, with values of 7.00 and 5.98 , respectively, compared with 4.28 and 3.94 for the upper OT. Undertoroidal-field ripple and a misalignment, the new upper horizontal target achieves a higher allowable average heat flux than the lower outer horizontal target (OHT), with values of 4.70 and 4.01 , respectively. These results show that magnetic ripple, assembly tolerances, and toroidal geometric continuity must be considered in the thermal design of divertor targets in fusion devices.

title: Wave-energy partition governs weak collisional damping in cold plasmas
abstract: Weak dissipation can control wave propagation, mode competition, and instability thresholds in plasmas, yet the physical origin of large branch-to-branch differences in collisional damping is often obscured by dielectric-tensor calculations. We show that weak collisional damping in cold plasmas is governed by wave-energy partition. In the one-rate cold plasma model with independent-relaxation collisions, the damping rate of a positive-energy collisionless eigenmode equals, to leading order in weak collisions, the collision frequency multiplied by the fraction of the total wave energy stored in plasma motion. This result recasts the standard perturbative damping formula into a compact and physically transparent law, immediately explaining why field-dominated branches such as whistlers can be much less damped than the collision frequency, whereas quasi-electrostatic modes can exhibit damping of comparable magnitude. Analytic examples for Langmuir, transverse electromagnetic, whistler, and extraordinary waves show that the energy-partition form classifies weak collisional damping across distinct branches and provides a simple diagnostic for mode competition in multibranch plasma-wave systems.

title: SOLPS-ITER simulation analysis on the synergistic effect of boron and neon in detached plasma on EAST
abstract: EAST experiments have demonstrated that combined neon (Ne) and boron (B) injection overcomes the narrow operational window of pure neon seeding, and compensates for the insufficient radiative capacity of B alone, establishing a stable ELM-suppressed H-mode with a partially detached outer divertor and good confinement (H98 ∼1) [Sun et al 2026 Nucl. Fusion66 044002]. To reveal the underlying physical mechanisms, SOLPS-ITER simulations of Ne–B co-injection are performed under EAST conditions. Three mechanisms are identified. First, B and Ne form a poloidal radiation synergy: Ne radiates efficiently at Te ∼20–27 eV near the X-point, while B fills the radiative gap below ∼17 eV in the divertor region, together extending the energy dissipation zone from the X-point to the target and enabling deep energy detachment. Second, the B-enhanced D+-D charge exchange in the near-scrape-off layer amplifies momentum loss and substantially reduces the target particle flux. Third, the reduced Ne seeding rate through compensating B radiation is the dominant lever for lowering core radiation and Zeff, because core impurity content is governed by Ne, with its density exceeding that of B by nearly two orders of magnitude regardless of injection rate. Additionally, the deeper detachment state further promotes B deposition on the divertor target, reinforcing wall conditioning. These mechanisms provide a generalizable physics framework for mixed low-Z/high-Z impurity injection strategies on ITER and future fusion devices.

title: AI-based plasma equilibrium parameter inference in KSTAR for DEMO-relevant reactors using only ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics
abstract: This study proposes a deep neural network for high-fidelity equilibrium parameter inference, serving as a surrogate of the magnetic EFIT reconstruction and relying exclusively on ex-vessel magnetic signals. The objective is to circumvent the long-term integrity constraints of in-vessel magnetic diagnostics in the nuclear environment of the Demonstration Fusion Power Reactor (DEMO)-relevant devices. Using KSTAR data (2021–2024), a baseline model trained solely on measured ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics (the Measurement-only model) is compared with an Augmented model, which addresses informational sparsity via virtual-sensor signals computed from the GEQDSK. The Augmented model achieves predictive fidelity comparable to off-line EFIT, with a coefficient of determination ( ) above and a range-normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE) of averaged over all parameters, against for the Measurement-only model. Because the virtual-sensor inputs derive from the EFIT solutions that define the targets, these figures quantify the surrogate fidelity with respect to the magnetic EFIT and constitute an upper bound on the accuracy attainable with physically installed ex-vessel probes, not that of an independent reconstruction. As the reference floor for the Measurement-only model, the magnetic fitting residuals of the parent EFIT reconstructions against the measured probe signals are quantified, yielding pooled range-normalized residuals of – per campaign with structured, campaign-persistent components that random noise perturbations do not emulate. Robust accuracy is maintained during neutral beam injection (NBI)-induced transients, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution verifies that the Augmented model captures the underlying magnetohydrodynamic physics, specifically the Shafranov shift. With a median single forward pass inference latency of ms (99th percentile: ms), the framework is a viable surrogate for conventional numerical solvers. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that an idealized, EFIT-consistent realization of a densified ex-vessel sensor configuration retains sufficient information for high-precision equilibrium parameter inference, provided that magnetic probes are physically installed at the designated locations. This establishes the information-content prerequisite for ex-vessel-only inference in DEMO. The accuracy attainable from physically installed probes, subject to conductor-model, calibration and structured measurement-model errors, is not established and requires validation against measured ex-vessel signals.

title: The multiscale nonlinear interactions between kinetic ballooning mode and drift wave turbulence critical for confinement improvement of hybrid fusion plasmas
abstract: Nonlinear suppression of short-wavelength drift wave turbulence by long-wavelength kinetic ballooning mode (KBM) in tokamak fusion plasma is proposed to be the main cause for confinement improvement in the core of hybrid fusion plasmas. Specifically, the ambient ion temperature gradient (ITG) turbulence, which can contribute considerable transport flux if not mitigated, is fully suppressed in the presence of KBM. KBM is demonstrated to be robustly unstable from fully electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. While its flux is low under low magnetic shear, KBM can generate significant stabilizing zonal flow whose velocity well surpasses the normalized linear growth rate (linear growth rate divided by its wave number) of ITG. This multiscale physics phenomenon is convincingly verified on a representative ASDEX-Upgrade hybrid scenario plasma.

title: System identification simulations using the advanced fluid neutral model and wide grid formalism in SOLPS-ITER
abstract: This work presents a first step towards using the SOLPS-ITER code package (Wiesen 2015 J. Nucl. Mater.463 480–4) for synthetic system identification (SysID) using multisine perturbations. Numerical modelling is used to replicate SysID experiments performed to establish exhaust control done on MAST-U (Kool 2025 Nat. Energy10 1116–31), (Van Berkel 2025 DPP 2025 (APS)). These experiments involve perturbing the gas injection rate and observing the Scrape-Off-Layer (SOL) response in the frequency domain. The model used is the Advanced Fluid Neutral (AFN) model of SOLPS-ITER (Horsten 2022 Nucl. Mater. Energy33 101247), implemented in the Wide Grids version of the code (Dekeyser 2021 Nucl. Mater. Energy27 100999). The grid was generated with the Grid Optimization and Adaptation Toolbox (Van den kerkhof 2024 Contrib. Plasma Phys.64 e202300134) and extends to the vessel wall, to enable calculating fluid neutral parameters across the entire domain. New boundary condition types were implemented in the code to allow for multisine gas injection perturbations, as well as reservoir models for remote vessel regions without plasma. In steady state, it is possible to simulate plasmas ranging from attached to deeply detached using different gas injection rates. This allows for comparison between simulation and experimental results at similar levels of detachment. Comparison between simulation and experimental data in the frequency domain shows that the AFN SOLPS-ITER simulations predict faster response times to divertor fuelling perturbations than the experiments, likely in part due to the fluid approximation used for the neutrals. When including the reservoir models for remote vessel regions the phase shifts increase, but are still too low compared to experiments.

title: Multi-beamlet operation of the ITER negative ion source prototype SPIDER towards full beam extraction
abstract: The neutral beam heating systems for ITER will be based on radio-frequency driven sources, accelerating a negative ion beam current of tens of amperes for up to one hour. In its second operation phase SO-2, the full-scale prototype source SPIDER was operated for the first time in multi-beamlet configuration at ∼70 kW driver−1, extracting a H—current density of 215 A m−2 over ¼ of the extraction area at 0.3 Pa source filling pressure, providing a total accelerated beam power of ∼700 kW. Scaling of the results confirms the specifications of the on-going RF generators upgrade, indicating that target current density of 330 A m−2 in hydrogen is achievable by increasing the RF power to 100 kW driver−1. Beam uniformity was assessed at the beamlet-group scale under moderate underperveance conditions: at high power row-averaged beamlet currents were within ±10% for fifteen out of sixteen rows. A lower homogeneity was observed at the single-beamlet level. The influence of the magnetic filter field on beam uniformity was also characterized, confirming the beneficial effect of multi-driver operation on homogeneity at the extraction region. A caesium conditioning procedure was developed and validated for the partial-source configuration. An anomalous amplification of the acceleration current peculiar of the vacuum-insulated source design specific to ITER sources, attributed to stray backstreaming charges and surface emission effects, was identified and mitigated by electrostatic shielding. Together with the ongoing installation of new solid-state RF generators and an improved pumping system, the results presented in this work open the way to full-source operation in the next experimental campaign and yield findings of direct relevance to the ITER injector design.

title: Electromagnetic gyrokinetic analysis in Tokamak Energy’s pre-concept design of the ST-E1 fusion power plant
abstract: ST-E1 is Tokamak Energy’s concept for a fusion power plant. As part of the pre-concept design, a series of reference flat-top plasma operating points have been developed and analysed in [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion66 086008)]. The present work focuses on the low-density baseline conceptual power plant (BCP) operating point of [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion66 086008)] selected as a representative operating point for the ST-E1 pilot plant and investigates its micro-stability, turbulent transport and transport-informed optimisation using first-principles spectral flux-tube electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. Linear gyrokinetic calculations, involving electrons, thermal ions, impurities, and thermal and fast helium ions, complemented by dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to identify subdominant and stable drift-wave eigenmodes, reveal two principal long-wavelength electromagnetic instability branches: hybrid h-ITG modes driven by thermal gradients and FI-KBMs, i.e. kinetic-ballooning-like modes strongly influenced by the plasma beta (a ratio of thermal to magnetic energy) and the fast-ion (FI) population. At shorter wavelengths, electron-temperature-gradient (ETG) modes become unstable towards the plasma edge while remaining stable in the core. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis identifies the principal equilibrium parameters governing these instabilities. Building on these linear predictions, nonlinear electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations are performed to quantify the resulting turbulent transport of the thermal plasma and fast helium ions. The reference operating point is found to exhibit saturated, rather than runaway, electromagnetic turbulence, establishing it as a physically meaningful baseline for further optimisation. The nonlinear simulations show that turbulent transport is governed primarily by the combined effects of the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, with intrinsic-rotation-driven shear providing an additional, complementary reduction in transport. Although fast ions provide the free energy driving the FI-KBM branch, increasing the fast-ion fraction is found to reduce the saturated turbulent transport across all species through nonlinear self-organisation. To efficiently explore the resulting multidimensional parameter space, defined by the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, a physics-informed interpolation framework constrained and validated by nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations has been developed, enabling the identification of transport-favourable operating points without requiring exhaustive nonlinear parameter scans. The resulting framework yields a family of transport-favourable operating points for the ST-E1 low-density BCP equilibrium and provides quantitative targets for future self-consistent equilibrium optimisation.

title: Composition-Dependent Dielectric Response and Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption in Sulfide/rGO Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Broadband electromagnetic wave absorption depends on the frequency dependence of the composite response, not simply on the magnitude of dielectric loss. Here, CuS, CoS, and CuCo2S4 are combined with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) at a fixed sulfide-to-carbon mass ratio to examine how sulfide composition affects dielectric response and thickness-dependent absorption. Compared with CoS@rGO and CuS@rGO, CuCo2S4@rGO exhibits superior electromagnetic wave absorption, which is attributed to the synergistic effects of interfacial polarization and balanced dielectric and magnetic losses. It achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.84 GHz at 2.4 mm and a minimum reflection loss of –46.7 dB at 2.9 mm. The CuCo2S4@rGO is also processed into poly(vinylidene fluoride) films. Electromagnetic measurements on stacked and pressed film specimens establish the response of the PVDF-based composite, while individual films show bendability, altered infrared thermal contrast, and self-extinguishing behavior under the tested conditions. This study relates sulfide-dependent dielectric response to broadband absorption and examines the processing of the absorber into a polymer composite.

title: Revisiting p- 11 ...
abstract: Recent experimental progress has substantially improved the available cross-section data for the p- B fusion reaction, particularly in energy regions that previously lacked direct measurements. In this study, we develop a high-precision analytical parameterization of the p- B reaction cross-section over the 0–10 MeV energy range, incorporating the new experimental data into a continuous and numerically efficient representation. Using this parameterization, we evaluate the thermonuclear reactivity of the p- B reaction and examine the effects of the dominant resonance at 0.6 MeV and a newly observed resonance around 4.7 MeV. Furthermore, we assess the energy balance by analyzing the fusion power density and the electron bremsstrahlung power density. Our results indicate that p- B fusion is not precluded by bremsstrahlung constraints when contemporary cross-section data and self-consistent thermal modeling are employed.

title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. Here, we report an Ir(III)-catalyzed nitrene-triggered aziridination–rearrangement cascade that enables the efficient conversion of cyclic-substituted tetrasubstituted alkenes into cycloalkane-fused δ-lactams. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir–nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

title: Clearing the way for a transformative stem-cell treatment for Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Most Parkinson’s therapies aim to reduce the motor-control symptoms that the disease triggers. But stem-cell transplants in the brain could alter the disease at a more fundamental level.

title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Vitrinite undergoes progressive structural ordering, whereas liptinite transforms more slowly at intermediate pressures owing to inherited defects and inhibited structural coalescence. Although both precursors respond strongly to pressure, their chemistry governs transitions between the processes that ultimately limit transformation rates. In this work, we develop a precursor-specific kinetic framework that integrates graphitization along geological pressure-temperature histories. Applications to representative Alpine tectonic units indicate that graphitization can continue during post-peak decompression or reheating. Precursor-dependent path integration further influences the modeled partitioning between graphite-like carbon and low-order reactive carbon fluxes. These results highlight how precursor chemistry and geological history jointly control carbon ordering, retention potential, and flux partitioning at convergent margins.

title: In-situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography and multiphysics modeling of the failure mechanisms in an end-of-vehicle-life lithium-ion battery upon indentation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face safety and reliability challenges throughout service and retirement. However, the mechanistic relationships among mechanically induced structural damage, internal short-circuit (ISC) initiation, and subsequent thermal behavior remain insufficiently understood. This study presents an integrated experimental and computational framework for investigating structural evolution and ISC behavior in an 18,650 cylindrical cell subjected to quasi-static indentation. By integrating in-situ structural characterization with coupled multiphysics modeling, the framework correlates internal deformation and interfacial failure with ISC initiation and localized thermal responses. In-situ synchrotron X-ray micro- computed tomography and stepwise indentation enabled three-dimensional visualization of electrode deformation, layer interaction, and interfacial delamination in an end-of-life (EoL) cell. A finite element model examined the mechanical response and stress distribution of the multilayered cell architecture and identified failure-prone regions under spherical indentation. The model was calibrated against the measured mechanical response and observed deformation, providing a basis for subsequent mechanistic analysis. Building on the mechanically calibrated model, a coupled mechanical-electrochemical-thermal framework was established to clarify the progression from indentation-induced deformation to ISC initiation and subsequent heat generation at different states of charge. The results illustrate that enhanced ductility of the jellyroll components and improved interfacial cohesion can limit failure propagation across adjacent electrode and separator layers, thereby improving structural integrity and reducing ISC risk. Moreover, indentation-induced ISC can cause a pronounced localized temperature rise and heat accumulation even at 30% state of charge, indicating that the associated safety risk remains non-negligible even at low charge levels. The proposed framework provides experimentally grounded insight into mechanically induced battery failure and informs safer cell design, second-life applications, and recycling.

title: Enhancing feasibility of cost-optimal energy systems in surrogate-assisted design optimization
abstract: Energy system design optimization often incurs high computational cost, which limits applications such as uncertainty analysis and interactive decision support. Surrogate models reduce this cost by emulating expensive original models. In surrogate-assisted design optimization (SADO), an upper-level optimization algorithm searches over designs while surrogate models emulate operational optimizations to evaluate each design. Existing SADO studies rarely enforce feasibility, defined here as the ability of an energy system to satisfy all demand constraints.This study quantifies how the choice of a feasibility predictor influences the cost and feasibility of designs obtained from SADO applied to a convex energy system model. We compare three feasibility predictors: two artificial neural networks and a convex hull predictor that classifies feasibility by membership in a feasible input space. We embed each predictor into SADO and evaluate predicted designs by their cost and feasibility when re-evaluated in the operational optimization.The results show that the feasibility predictor strongly affects both cost and feasibility of designs. SADO with neural-network-based feasibility predictors achieves feasible designs consistently only if oversizing is enforced. In contrast, SADO with the convex hull predictor yields guaranteed feasible designs by construction and produces designs whose objective values are typically within 2 % of the cost-optimal solution. This improved feasibility comes at the expense of increased computational cost compared to neural-network-based feasibility predictors. Overall, these results establish feasibility prediction as a critical design choice in SADO and identify geometric feasibility predictors as robust alternatives to data-driven surrogate models for convex energy system models.

title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

title: Autoantibodies associate with clinical outcome in patients with melanoma treated with a dendritic cell-based vaccine
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Increased B cell receptor signaling pathways in patients with melanoma correlates with a favorable clinical response to a cancer vaccine expressing multiple tumor-associated antigens. Here, we utilize phage immunoprecipitation sequencing (PhIP-seq) and Rapid Extracellular Antigen Profiling (REAP) assays to analyze the autoantibody profiles of patients with melanoma from a dendritic cell vaccine trial (NCT01622933), before and after vaccination. Patients have significantly elevated breadth and titer of autoantibodies compared to healthy donors. Vaccination results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies, particularly those with a favorable clinical outcome. Reduced serum SDF1-alpha, MIP-1ß, MCP1 and increased circulating monocytes are associated with development of autoantibodies. We identify plasma autoantibody signatures separating melanoma from healthy subjects as well as clinical responders vs non-responders to vaccination treatment. These findings demonstrate the potential for autoantibodies as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers that predict clinical outcomes in cancer.

title: Electrochemical Capture and Accumulation of Uranium Using a Layered Uvanite Electrode
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. Building on a comprehensive understanding of charge-transfer and transport mechanisms, we found that potentiodynamic modulation enables selective capture of uranium species using a uvanite electrode. By allowing competing cations to deintercalate at lower potentials and preventing proton deintercalation, UO3 dissolution is inhibited, achieving a high UO3 recovery capacity of 515 mg/g at 10 times the competing cation concentration. The new electrochemistry of the uvanite electrode helps develop cost-effective, sustainable battery electrodes for critical ion extraction from water.

title: Covalent-Bond Engineering Stabilizes Layered Oxide Cathodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.

title: Light-Driven Hydrogenation–Dehydrogenation of Toluene–Methylcyclohexane by Plasmonic Photocatalysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of an efficient and reversible hydrogen storage and transport system is crucial for a sustainable hydrogen economy. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a potential solution due to their high hydrogen storage density and ease of transport, but conventional thermal approaches for the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of LOHCs remain heavily reliant on harsh operating conditions. Here, we demonstrate a plasmonic photocatalysis approach for toluene hydrogenation to methylcyclohexane and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation to toluene under substantially milder conditions. We observe changes in reaction orders and substantial reductions in activation barriers by 0.34 and 1.11 eV for toluene hydrogenation and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, respectively, as compared to thermocatalysis due to the role of hot carriers. Both reactions exhibit high activity, stability (>70 h), and excellent selectivity (>95%), offering a sustainable pathway for on-demand hydrogen storage and release.

title: Decoding microprotein interactome via a minimal genetically encoded photocatalytic proximity labeling system
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microproteins (typically E. coli, mammalian cells, C. elegans and Arabidopsis thaliana establishes FlashID as a complementary, minimally perturbative platform for decoding microprotein interaction networks in vivo and advancing photocatalytic proximity labeling technologies.

title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

title: A nanomolar-affinity antibody enabling sensitive labeling and high-resolution genomic mapping of O-GlcNAc
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-affinity O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc)-specific antibodies are crucial for the sensitive detection and functional study of O-GlcNAcylation. Here, we report the development of a nanomolar-affinity O-GlcNAc antibody named EPR19847 by using a degenerate O-GlcNAcylated peptide as the immunogen. The EPR19847 antibody can be used for O-GlcNAc detection, imaging, isolation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Using this antibody, O-GlcNAcylated proteins are enriched and identified in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by next-generation sequencing demonstrates that O-GlcNAc is enriched around the promoters of highly expressed genes, and that its genomic distribution is positively correlated with transcription-activating marks including H3K4me3, H3K9ac, and RNA polymerase II in mESCs. Further analysis suggests a high occupancy of O-GlcNAcylation within super-enhancers. We anticipate that EPR19847 will serve as a powerful tool for the highly sensitive detection and systematic functional dissection of O-GlcNAc.

title: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Computational and mathematical models are frequently used in the design of appropriate experimental protocols for in vitro cell differentiation assays. However, models are limited by typical monotonic dose-responses, preventing them from being used for cytokine effects that are largely non-monotonic. To address this shortcoming, we developed Uncovering Non-Monotonic Antagonistic and Synergistic Combinations (UNMASC), a mathematical model describing non-monotonic dose-response surfaces of cytokine interactions that distinguishes synergy of efficacy and potency. We demonstrate that our approach successfully recapitulates non-monotonic observed dose-response surfaces characterizing in vitro T cell progenitor differentiation. Our results show that interleukin (IL)3 and IL7 have antagonistic effects alone but are synergistic in combination. Altogether, UNMASC can aid in the efficient design of cell generation assays and extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7. Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

title: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses. Macrophage-mediated inflammation is central to the pathology, and it is important to understand the epigenetic mechanisms involved. By screening epigenetic molecules that are differentially expressed in published human IBD datasets, we find Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) consistently downregulated in IBD samples compared to healthy controls. Co-occurrence of Prmt6 suppression and Il1b induction within the myeloid compartment in colon biopsy samples indicates that PRMT6 limits macrophage-driven inflammation. Concordantly, Prmt6-deficient mice exhibit increased susceptibility to both DSS- and TNBS-induced colitis, characterized by exacerbated tissue damage and systemic elevation of IL-1β. Transcriptomic profiling confirms that PRMT6 deficiency selectively upregulates Il1b among inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, PRMT6 suppresses Il1b transcription by interacting with RBBP5 and disrupting SET1A complex assembly, thereby reducing H3K4me3 enrichment at the Il1b promoter, independently of its canonical H3R2me2a catalytic activity. Furthermore, PRMT6 is transcriptionally silenced by the NF-κB subunit p50 during inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of p50 restores PRMT6 expression, thus protecting mice from DSS-induced colitis in a PRMT6-dependent manner. Our findings highlight PRMT6 as a pivotal epigenetic regulator of the inflammatory response and provide proof of principle for targeting the p50–PRMT6–IL-1β axis in IBD.

title: Colonic enterochromaffin cells modulate a neuronal-immune-epithelial cell axis for antimicrobial homeostasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The intestinal mucosa functions alongside trillions of commensal microbes, with immune and epithelial responses contributing to microbiota homeostasis. Both immune and nerve cells are implicated in this microbial balance, but the regulatory functions of epithelial enteroendocrine cells (EEC) are not understood well. Here we show that EEC depletion in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency enhances goblet cell expression of prominent antimicrobial peptides, with stronger effects in female than in male mice. Mechanistically, serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) derived from enterochromaffin (EC) cells, an EEC-subtype, acts on sensory neurons to suppress the mucosal levels of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) under physiological conditions. In the absence of local serotonin, elevated CGRP levels promote mast cell infiltration and interleukin-13 (IL-13) secretion in EEC-depleted mice and enhance antimicrobial gene expression in goblet cells. Our findings thus delineate an epithelial–neuronal–immune axis, wherein EC cells fine-tune goblet cell antimicrobial output to preserve gut microbial equilibrium.

title: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

title: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) prevents excessive protein aggregation and mediates aggrephagy by modulating the liquidity of p62 condensates
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Loss of proteostasis can cause protein aggregation and trigger aggrephagy, yet how these biological processes are coordinated remains unclear. Here, we showed that p62 condensates transit from a gel-like to a more liquid-like state in response to proteotoxic stress. VHL was recruited to aggresomes and colocalizes with p62, which is crucial for p62 to perform its distinct functions in aggresome formation and autophagic degradation. Mechanistically, VHL binds to p62 through its IDR1 region and increases the liquid-like properties via IDR2 region. VHL depletion or disease-associated IDR2 mutations impair p62 condensate dynamics, leading to excessive accumulation of aggregated proteins and concomitant KEAP1 sequestration/NRF2 stabilization. A chimeric peptide linking the p62 PB1 domain to VHL IDR2 recapitulates VHL’s fluidity-promoting activity and suppresses tumorigenesis and protein aggregation. Overall, our findings reveal an HIF-independent tumor-suppressive role of VHL in regulating proteostasis and suggest a new treatment for cancer through the targeting of condensate dynamics.

title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1-deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

title: Global MORBs reveal a warmer present-day ambient mantle and moderate secular cooling of Earth
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Earth’s mantle temperature controls melting, crust formation and planetary cooling, but its present-day ambient value remains debated. Most geodynamic models assume ~1350 ± 50 °C, calibrated indirectly from experiments and the 6–7 km thickness of oceanic crust. Here we show, using primary-magma thermobarometry on >16,000 mid-ocean ridge basalts—seafloor lavas erupted where tectonic plates diverge—that only ~1% preserve primitive compositions that constrain mantle temperature. Under reduced redox conditions, these melts imply ~1421 °C, a value that would generate crust much thicker than seismic observations unless part of the melt is retained or crystallizes below the seafloor. title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m−2 yr−1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m−2 yr−1. Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km2), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr−1. title: Na-Layer K+ Pillaring with CeO2 Coating Enables High-Rate and Air-Stable P2-Type NaMn-Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract P2-type NaxMnO2 cathodes offer high capacity and elemental abundance, yet their practical application is limited by the Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+ and irreversible phase transitions that drive structural degradation, capacity fading, and air sensitivity. Prevailing strategies rely predominantly on element substitution at transition-metal sites, whether via single or dual doping, or in combination with coating, but inevitably impose a capacity–stability trade-off rooted in the alteration of the TM–O framework. Here, we demonstrate a synergistic strategy to construct a high-rate, air-stable P2-Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode, by combining K+ bulk doping at Na sites with a CeO2 surface coating. The K+ bulk doping mitigates the Jahn–Teller effect, eliminates the low-voltage P2–P′2 transition, and converts the high-voltage P2–OP4 transition into a solid-solution reaction, while the CeO2 overlayer concurrently provides resistance to ambient air. The optimized Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode delivers 67.95 mAh g–1 at 10C, retains 84.00% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 1C and 71.03% after 500 cycles at 5C, and preserves structural integrity after air exposure and water immersion. This dual-modification approach establishes Na-site doping as a design principle that decouples structural stabilization from transition-metal redox activity in P2-type oxide cathodes.

title: Construction of Multivariate Hierarchical Metal–Organic Framework/Polymer Composites by Redox Concomitant Reconstitution Method for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rational design of metal–organic framework/polymer (MOF/polymer) composites featuring integrated architectures and synergistic functionalities represents an effective strategy for developing advanced materials whose emergent properties outperform those of individual components. Herein, we report a Redox Concomitant Reconstitution (RCR) strategy that enables the concomitant structural reconstitution of metastable MOFs and in situ polymer functionalization, resulting in hierarchical MOF/polymer composites with structure-function synergy. Upon exposure to a mixed methanol/pyrrole vapor, the metastable CuCo-PC precursor is structurally reconstituted into hierarchical CuCo-MOF-74 enriched with Cu(0)/Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Co(II) multimetallic sites, while pyrrole is concomitantly oxidatively polymerized into a conformal polypyrrole (PPy) layer, yielding CuCo-MOF-74/PPy composites with integrated architecture and functionality. Benefiting from the synergy among the multimetallic catalytic sites, hierarchical porosity, and PPy photothermal layer, the composite achieves a 96% yield in the photothermal catalytic CO2 cycloaddition using sterically hindered long-chain epoxides and maintains robust stability over 10 consecutive cycles. This work establishes the RCR strategy as a versatile platform for constructing advanced multifunctional MOF/polymer composites with tailored architectures and synergistic functionalities, opening new opportunities for solar-driven CO2 valorization and the rational design of next-generation MOF-based hybrid materials.

title: An accessible Python framework for real-time magnetic tweezers microscope control and image processing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnetic tweezers are a popular biophysical instrument for manipulating and measuring single molecules. Most groups rely on custom-built setups tailored to specific experiments, making it challenging to implement and share software. Typically, image acquisition and hardware control are automated via LabVIEW, while real-time video processing is implemented in C + + /CUDA libraries. Live processing can eliminate the need to store raw video, enabling high throughput, fast acquisition rates, and simplified experimental workflows. However, no open-source general-purpose software framework currently unifies these capabilities for magnetic tweezers experiments. Here, we introduce MagTrack and MagScope open-source Python-based tools designed to fill this gap. MagTrack is an image-processing library that efficiently determines bead positions from magnetic-tweezers videos using CPU or GPU computation. MagScope is a comprehensive software framework offering a graphical user interface, real-time hardware control, data acquisition, and video processing. It is built on a multiprocessing architecture for responsive, high-throughput computation. Together, MagTrack and MagScope offer a fully customizable, end-to-end, open-source Python alternative to proprietary or fragmented systems, enabling laboratories to adapt and extend the framework according to their experimental needs.

title: Composition-Dependent Atomic Layer Etching of Multicomponent Oxide Semiconductors with Preserved Electrical Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for next-generation memory device scaling, owing to their low off-state current, low-temperature processability, and excellent compatibility with back-end-of-line manufacturing. Here, we report the composition-dependent atomic layer etching (ALE) behavior of the multicomponent oxide semiconductor InGaZnOx (IGZO), enabled by a hydrogen-based surface modification chemistry. The constituent cations of IGZO exhibit markedly different reactivities toward hydrogen, allowing the overall etch rate to be systematically tuned through elemental composition. Because this reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, ALE minimizes damage to the underlying front-channel region, achieving atomic-scale material removal with minimal degradation of electrical performance, in contrast to conventional dry-etching approaches that often degrade transistor characteristics. Leveraging this low-damage, self-limiting characteristic, we further demonstrate that ALE enables post-deposition trimming of nonuniform IGZO films conformally deposited within three-dimensional trench structures, improving step coverage to nearly 100%. These results establish hydrogen-based ALE as a versatile, composition-aware process for the atomic-scale control of multicomponent oxide semiconductor channels, offering a low-damage route toward scalable three-dimensional memory device architectures.

title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

abstract: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.
