This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.

title: Multiscale Magnetic–Dielectric Coupling in Bidirectionally Aligned Multilayer Graphene/FeSiAl Aerogels for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lightweight electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbers with broad attenuation bandwidths are highly desirable for electromagnetic protection and stealth applications, yet their development is limited by the persistent trade-off between impedance matching and attenuation capability. Although aligned porous architectures have been widely explored to enhance electromagnetic dissipation, most existing strategies rely on unidirectional or single-component alignment and rarely enable the coordinated orientation of magnetic and dielectric phases together with macroscopic impedance grading. Herein, bidirectionally aligned graphene/FeSiAl/polyimide aerogels with coupled micro- and macroscale architectures are fabricated through magnetic-field-assisted directional freezing. At the microscale, a horizontal magnetic field orients ferromagnetic FeSiAl flakes, whereas a vertical temperature gradient directs the alignment of graphene/polyimide cell walls, forming an orthogonally ordered magnetic-dielectric network that promotes conductive loss, interfacial/dipolar polarization, and magnetic dissipation while regulating impedance matching. The optimized single-layer aerogel achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.13 GHz at only 1.32 mm, representing a 52.49% improvement over its temperature-gradient-only counterpart, together with a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –57.35 dB at 1.74 mm. At the macroscale, layer-by-layer freezing constructs multilayer aerogels, enabling broadband EMW entry and progressive energy dissipation. The optimized multilayer aerogel delivers an ultrabroad EAB of 12.49 GHz and an RLmin of –54.23 dB, yielding a pronounced radar cross-section reduction of 34.08 dB under normal incidence. This multiscale coupling strategy provides an effective route toward lightweight, thin, and broadband EMW absorbers.

title: Dynamic Decoupling as a Strategy for Highly Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a promising sustainable alternative to conventional industrial production. Nonetheless, its practical efficiency is fundamentally capped by the inherent coupling of catalytic kinetics, interfacial electric field, and mass transport, becoming a critical bottleneck for classical static electrolysis strategies. Here, a dynamic decoupling strategy (i.e., a temporal separation of the dominant interfacial constraint rather than a physical decoupling of involved processes) is introduced and validated on a Co-ONx-C single-atom-catalyst-based cathode, employing pulsed electrolysis to modulate the coupled processes in the time domain. This dynamic approach engineers the electrocatalytic interface through three time-separated effects of unequal weight: mass-transport replenishment during the rest interval predominantly enhances H2O2 accumulation, interfacial-field modulation across the potential of zero charge governs the selectivity improvement, and support-defect modulation enables efficient Co-site utilization. As a result, this unconventional approach promotes a 2.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 concentration over the static mode, significantly suppressing the parasitic H2 evolution reaction. Validated in a photovoltaic-driven system with over 100 day stable production, this work establishes dynamic decoupling as a smart design principle for next-generation environmental electrocatalysis.

title: Light-Responsive Hybrid Lipid Nanoparticles with Gold Nanorods for Light-Triggered DNA Delivery
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Gene therapy is a cutting-edge strategy for treating, preventing, and potentially eradicating a wide range of diseases. Its success is critically dependent on the transfection efficiency of gene delivery systems. In this context, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely investigated for the delivery of plasmid DNA. However, their performance still lacks precise spatiotemporal control. To address this limitation, we present a novel plasmonic hybrid delivery system composed of gold nanorods (AuNRs) assembled on the LNP surface. This architecture integrates the efficient delivery properties of LNPs with the optical responsiveness of AuNRs, enabling the light-induced release of plasmid DNA upon near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation. The morphology of AuNRs was specifically tailored to achieve photothermal (PT) heating under NIR laser excitation, thereby enabling PT-assisted regulation of transfection. Thermo-optical, physicochemical, and morphological analyses confirm that LNP/AuNRs display the desired features, including an absorption band centered at 860 nm, a unimodal size distribution, and a positive surface charge. Ultrastructural evaluation by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals cellular internalization of LNP/AuNRs and robust plasmid DNA transfection following NIR laser irradiation. PT heating significantly enhances transfection efficiency in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells compared to nonirradiated samples. Biomimetic assays using anionic liposomes revealed that NIR-triggered DNA release is facilitated by nanoparticle–membrane interactions, likely involving structural destabilization of the hybrid system under PT activation. Time-lapse imaging and multichannel confocal microscopy revealed that NIR-induced PT activation modulates the intracellular dynamics of LNP/AuNRs by reducing lysosomal association and promoting a more diffusive behavior, potentially contributing to enhanced cargo availability and transfection efficiency. These findings demonstrate the multifunctional properties of LNP/AuNRs as an efficient, light-responsive platform for PT-triggered plasmid DNA delivery, opening a new avenue for on-demand gene therapy.

title: Reactive Oxygen Species-Scavenging Nanozyme Hydrogel for Microenvironment Modulation in Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic chronic wounds are difficult to heal because persistent hyperglycemia is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), impaired angiogenesis, and prolonged inflammation. Here, we developed an Fe3O4@PDA-containing PVA/gelatin/borate hydrogel (FP-PVG) with catalase-like activity. FP-PVG scavenged ROS and promoted H2O2-responsive oxygen generation, while the FP nanocomposite and hydrogel matrix contributed to antibacterial activity. In vitro, FP-PVG showed strong ABTS radical-scavenging activity (98.97% at 2 mg mL–1), favorable cytocompatibility, and improved cell migration under oxidative stress. It also reduced CD86 expression and increased CD163 expression in macrophages, consistent with a shift toward a reparative phenotype. In a diabetic mouse wound model, FP-PVG accelerated wound closure and was associated with reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, increased angiogenesis, and improved tissue regeneration. These findings support FP-PVG as a multifunctional hydrogel dressing for regulating the diabetic wound microenvironment.

title: Polymer-Passivated ZnO Microcluster Arrays for High-Responsivity, Low-Voltage UV Photodetection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal-oxide UV photodetectors typically require elevated bias to achieve high sensitivity, limiting their suitability for low-power and portable applications. Here, we demonstrate poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)-engineered zinc oxide (ZnO) nano-microcluster arrays (NMCAs) that deliver outstanding UV photodetection performance at a low operating voltage of 0.1 V. The optimized device exhibited a high responsivity of 376 mA W–1, representing an ∼8.5-fold enhancement over pristine NMCA-structured ZnO under identical testing conditions, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Controlled PMMA infiltration progressively modulates surface defects and interparticle charge-transport pathways in these mechanically robust, liquid-sintered NMCAs, with the performance enhancement primarily arising from defect passivation rather than optical absorption changes. Structural and spectroscopic analyses suggest that controlled PMMA infiltration modifies the polymer–oxide interface without altering the intrinsic wurtzite ZnO crystal structure, with the enhanced response primarily attributed to PMMA-assisted defect passivation and improved carrier lifetime. A clear responsivity-speed trade-off emerges with increasing polymer loading, whereby intermediate PMMA content yields effective defect passivation and maximum responsivity, while excessive infiltration introduces transport bottlenecks. The relatively slow rise and decay times indicate that these devices are better suited to static or quasi-static UV monitoring rather than high-speed photodetection. Moreover, by enhancing UV photoresponse at a very low operating voltage of 0.1 V through rational polymer–oxide interfacial engineering, this scalable approach provides a promising strategy for battery-compatible UV monitoring and porous metal-oxide optoelectronic systems.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: Bioinspired Curvature-Driven Droplet Transport on Slippery Lubricant-Infused Elastomeric Surfaces for Efficient Passive Fog Collection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric fog harvesting is a promising route for decentralized water production, yet its efficiency remains limited by droplet pinning and dissipative transport. Here, we address these constraints through a bioinspired strategy that integrates cactus-like conical geometries with slippery lubricant-infused elastomeric (SLIE) coatings based on PDMS–silicone oil networks to regulate droplet dynamics. The SLIE interfaces exhibit consistently low contact angle hysteresis across liquids of varying surface tensions, confirming robust omniphobicity. Unlike conventional liquid-infused surfaces, the PDMS-based slippery elastomeric interfaces eliminate observable droplet cloaking and exhibit low contact angle hysteresis, promoting sustained low-dissipation droplet transport suitable for fog harvesting. This synergy between surface chemistry and geometric asymmetry results in a significant enhancement in fog harvesting performance. SLIE-functionalized conical substrates achieve up to (∼150%) higher water collection rates compared to hydrophilic controls, driven by reduced viscoelastic resistance and accelerated droplet shedding. Furthermore, decreasing cone apex angles (5°–10°) amplifies Laplace pressure gradients, leading to earlier droplet mobilization and improved collection efficiencies relative to larger cone angle geometries (30°–45°). These findings establish a mechanistic design framework that integrates omniphobic liquid interfaces with curvature-induced transport, providing a scalable strategy for next-generation passive water harvesting systems.

title: Shape-Memory Photonic–Plasmonic Crystals for Programmable Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful analytical technique for ultrasensitive molecular detection. Integrating photonic architectures with plasmonic nanostructures provides an effective strategy to enhance SERS by exploiting slow-photon effects. However, continuously and reversibly controlling photonic enhancement remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a shape-memory photonic–plasmonic crystal (SMPPC) that enables programmable slow-photon signal enhancement through reversible structural reconstruction. By exploiting its shape-memory properties, the optical response of SMPPC can be reversibly modulated through solution evaporation or mechanical contact. Structural reconstruction dynamically modulates the spectral detuning between the excitation wavelength and the photonic stopband edge, resulting in a nonmonotonic SERS response governed by the interplay between plasmonic hotspot evolution and slow-photon effect. The fully recovered SMPPC substrate delivers an 8.1-fold enhancement in SERS intensity compared with the plasmonic copolymer SERS substrate. As a proof of concept, the SMPPC substrate enables the detection of antibiotics in municipal wastewater effluents at concentrations down to 471 ppt. This work establishes shape-memory-enabled photonic reconfiguration as a strategy for programmable manipulation of SERS, opening new opportunities for adaptive photonic–plasmonic sensing platforms.

title: Predicting battery stability from electron-ion transport mismatch
abstract: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.

title: Entropy–Enthalpy Synergistic Quinary A-Site Engineering for High-Luminance and Stable Green Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multicomponent A-site engineering is effective in enhancing perovskite crystallization and optoelectronic performance, yet the cooperative mechanism of different cations in regulating crystallization kinetics remains unclear. Here, we propose an entropy–enthalpy synergistic quinary A-site strategy to modulate the crystallization of green 3D perovskites. By sequentially incorporating MA+, GA+, Cs+, and Rb+ into FAPbBr3, we constructed binary to quinary systems. This approach synergistically lowers the Gibbs free energy (ΔG), strengthens the thermodynamic driving force, and reduces the nucleation barrier (ΔG*), leading to dense and uniform nucleation as well as optimized crystal growth. The quinary device achieves a maximum luminance of 222,973 cd m–2 and maintains an External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) above 8% across 30,000–170,000 cd m–2. The peak luminance and maximum EQE are improved by approximately 12-fold and 20-fold, respectively, compared to the unary control. The device also exhibits an operational half-lifetime (T50) of 80 min at 13,000 cd m–2, corresponding to a projected lifetime of 1.47 × 104 h at 100 cd m–2. This work elucidates the synergistic role of multicomponent A-site cations in crystallization control and offers a promising route toward high-luminance brightness and stable 3D Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes (PeLEDs).

title: Interfacial Doping and Band Bending Boosting Thermoelectric Power Factor in 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 Quantum-Dot Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Superlattice films are promising candidates for obtaining excellent thermoelectric performance because the hetero-interface can effectively regulate both carrier and phonon transport. However, the atomic and electronic structures at the hetero-interface remain largely unexplored, limiting the deep understanding of interfacial effects. Here, 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 quantum-dot films were fabricated for investigating the 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 hetero-interface and its effect on electrical transport. Atomic-scale characterizations indicate apparent Mo doping at the hetero-interface, while band structure calculations and transport measurements reveal that Mo doping can reconstruct the conduction band and enhance band degeneracy, leading to a large carrier effective mass of ∼1.6 m0. Meanwhile, spectroscopy measurements verify donor-like states and local band bending at the hetero-interface, which introduce modulation doping and thereby enable synergistically optimized electron density and carrier mobility. As a result, the best (1T′-MoTe2)0.8(Bi2Te3)12 film achieves a peak power factor of ∼3.74 mW m–1 K–2 at 325 K. These findings provide new insights of interfacial effects on synergistically optimizing carrier transport and electrical properties of thermoelectric superlattice or quantum-dot films.

title: How the brain protects itself from Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Brains are resilient. Harnessing their self-protective mechanisms might help to prevent or slow the progression of this neurodegenerative condition.

title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

title: Spatially Confined Protein Condensates Enable Sustainable Food Manufacturing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Escalating climate pressures paired with rapid global population expansion threaten long-term animal protein security. The global plant-based protein market, presently valued at US$20–22.5 billion, is forecast to expand to US$38–43 billion by the early 2030s, signaling a robust translational demand for scalable, sustainable manufacturing of alternative proteins. However, most alternative proteins are featured by intrinsic colloidal instability, limiting their deployment in tailor-made viscoelastic food materials. This work establishes spatially confined liquid–liquid phase separation (SCLLPS) as a versatile approach towards viscoelastic protein manufacturing. Kinetically, driven by synergistic surface patch interactions and volume exclusion effects, proteins at a high loading (15.0 wt %) undergo selective phase partitioning and become spatially entrapped within anionic domains of polysaccharide matrices. Thermodynamically, the release of cavity-wrap water and retention of bound water jointly provide the energetic driving force forming protein-enriched liquid condensates with long-term colloidal stability. Mechanically, such spatially ordered condensates afford exceptional control over bulk viscoelasticity to tailor fluid mechanics, addressing a long-standing challenge to date. The broad generality of SCLLPS is verified across diverse plant and fungal proteins coupled with distinct anionic polysaccharides, delivering a universal condensate-tuning platform for low-impact food manufacturing with drastically reduced carbon, water, and land footprints.

title: Photocatalytic therapy via cross-coupling hydrogen evolution in cancer cells
abstract: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.

title: Bi3+/Ln3+-Codoped Boroaluminate Phosphors with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Multidimensional Luminescence Readout and UV-Shielding
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Combining lattice regulation of crystal-field-sensitive Bi3+ emission with Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization provides two complementary pathways for tuning the luminescence of single-host phosphors. Herein, Bi3+-activated Sr6Lu1-yYyAl(BO3)6 solid solutions and Bi3+/Ln3+-codoped Sr6LuAl(BO3)6 (SLAB; Ln = Eu, Dy, Sm, and Tb) phosphors were synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction. SLAB:Bi3+ exhibited broadband blue-violet emission centered at 419 nm under 325 nm excitation. Isovalent Y3+ substitution for Lu3+ regulated the local environment of Bi3+ and enhanced the integrated emission intensity by approximately sixfold under 365 nm excitation, with internal and external quantum efficiencies (IQE and EQE) reaching 87.2 and 31.7%, respectively. The lifetime-derived efficiency of Bi3+ → Eu3+ energy transfer reached a maximum of 85.8% and enabled continuous color tuning from blue-violet to orange-red by adjusting the Eu3+ concentration and excitation wavelength. Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization was further demonstrated for Dy3+, Sm3+, and Tb3+, producing purple, purplish-red, and green emissions, respectively. Taking advantage of their strong UV absorption, the phosphors were incorporated into flexible films for a proof-of-concept evaluation of UV shielding. The tunable multicolor emissions were further used to fabricate multicolor security labels and demonstrate binary optical encryption. Differential thermal quenching of Bi3+ and Sm3+ emissions enabled ratiometric thermometry over 298–573 K, with maximum absolute and relative sensitivities of 6.55 × 10–2 K–1 and 1.07% K–1, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-host boroaluminate phosphors for multidimensional luminescence readout, optical thermometry, and UV-shielding applications.

title: Synergistic Interface Engineering of Dopamine and SDBS for Constructing High-Performance Graphene/Sponge Composites With Enhanced Stability and Sensitivity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite significant advances in sponge-based pressure sensors for wearable devices and human–machine interfaces, achieving a sponge composite that simultaneously delivers ultrahigh sensitivity, a broad detection range and long-term mechanical stability remain a critical challenge, largely owing to the weak interfacial adhesion between the conductive nanofiller and the sponge skeleton. Herein, we demonstrate a robust interface engineering strategy for a multifunctional composite essentially consisting of a polydopamine (PDA)-modified polyurethane (PU) sponge and sodium dodecyl benzenesulfonate (SDBS)-functionalized graphene. The PDA coating affords a positively charged surface rich in catechol and amino groups, whereas SDBS imparts negative charges and stable dispersibility to graphene. First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the interfacial interactions and electronic structure evolution between the PDA@PU sponge and Gr@SDBS nanosheets, revealing synergistic hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction that ensure strong adhesion and uniform graphene decoration. Such a robust interface established by multiple noncovalent interactions facilitates the conformal and uniform decoration of graphene onto the 3D PU skeleton, thereby establishing a highly stable and continuous conductive pathway. The resulting Gr@SDBS/DPA@PU sponge composite delivers an outstanding sensitivity (6.46 kPa–1), a wide detection range (up to 550 kPa), a rapid response time (31.1 ms), and exceptional cyclic stability (up to 5000 cycles). Furthermore, by integrating a miniaturized wireless Bluetooth module, the sensor enables accurate real-time monitoring of finger joint movements and wireless gesture-based remote human-machine interaction. This work provides mechanistic insights into interface engineering of graphene/sponge composites and establishes a novel paradigm for smart wearable electronics.

title: Over 95% Optical Reflectance From Structurally Modulated All‐Biopolymer Multilayers
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable photonics aims to replace conventional optical materials with environmentally benign alternatives, yet its development is fundamentally constrained by the narrow intrinsic refractive‐index variability of biopolymers. Here we show that a dense–porous periodic architecture yields nearly perfect optical reflection using only polysaccharides. By exploiting the difference in skeletal rigidity between amorphous pectin and crystalline cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), we form alternating dense, high‐refractive‐index pectin layers and porous, low‐refractive‐index CNF layers through a combination of electrodeposition with solvent exchange. This dense–porous periodic architecture yields reflectivities exceeding 97% in the visible range and 95% in the near‐infrared—a range unprecedented for biopolymer‐based optical materials. Moreover, the strategy is simple, scalable, and highly versatile, enabling free spectral design across the visible and near‐infrared regions, broadband metallic‐like reflection, and planar patterning within a single fabrication process. Combined with the low thermal conductivity arising from porous layers and the coexistence of visible transparency and near‐infrared reflection, the resulting films show potential as transparent thermal‐management materials. This work establishes a new materials design principle for biodegradable, polysaccharide‐based photonic systems and advances the field of sustainable photonics.

title: Maximum Stability Point Tracking Stabilizes Wide‐Bandgap Mixed‐Halide Perovskite Solar Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Perovskite Solar Cells In article number e71358, Mansoo Choi, Yun Seog Lee, Namyoung Ahn, and co-workers report maximum stability point tracking (MSPT) for wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite solar cells. Trapped-charge accumulation is identified as a key factor driving halide segregation during operation. By mitigating charge accumulation, MSPT enables devices to retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation.

title: Multifunctional Matrix‐Activated Electrodes Enabling Efficient Proton Transport and Durable Low‐Pt Operation for High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells In article number e71438, Hansung Kim, Katie Heeyum Lim, So Young Lee, and co-workers introduce a cerium hydrogen phosphate-integrated multifunctional matrix-activated electrode that transforms the catalyst-layer microenvironment in high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The matrix strengthens proton-conduction networks, suppresses radical-driven degradation, and fortifies the porous catalyst-layer architecture, enabling remarkably durable, high-performance operation at reduced Pt loading.

title: Engineering Topological Phases in Two‐Dimensional Materials: A Path from Preparation to Device Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two‐dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase‐engineered material platforms.

title: Hydro‐Gated Photonic Actuators With Programmable Color and Shape
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural color actuators integrating visual readout with motion are prized for biomimicry, yet typically operate in a coupled, color‐gradient mode with limited freedom. Here we report a photonic liquid crystal network that decouples these responses via a scattering‐gated mechanism. The material hides its structural color in the dry state but, upon water uptake, simultaneously switches on vivid coloration and executes programmable three‐dimensional deformation. Crucially, we achieve stimulus‐selective control: ethanol turns on color without motion, while heat induces motion without color. This independent, on‐demand manipulation of optical and mechanical outputs offers a transformative platform for multi‐responsive soft robotics, adaptive camouflage, and smart displays.

title: Planar Focusing of Anisotropic Plasmon Polaritons in MoOCl 2 /Au
abstract: ABSTRACT Hyperbolic polaritons offer a promising approach for subwavelength light confinement and manipulation. While extensively explored across mid‐infrared to terahertz bands, achieving long‐distance focusing at visible frequencies remains challenging due to the trade‐off between long propagation and strong compression. In this work, we demonstrate planar focusing of anisotropic plasmon polaritons with an extended focal length in a MoOCl 2 /Au heterostructure. By integrating an Au metastructure with the natural hyperbolic material MoOCl 2 , we convert surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) into surface plasmon hyperbolic polaritons (SPHPs), enabling excitation and focusing of the low‐momentum hybrid anisotropic polariton in the heterostructure. Furthermore, by optimizing the thickness of the MoOCl 2 layer, we synergistically enhance both the propagation distance and the field compression. Using transmission‐mode scanning near‐field optical microscopy (SNOM) and quantitative methods, we demonstrate a focal length of 2.5λ and a focal spot with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of λ /5 under 633 nm excitation, accompanied by a threefold energy enhancement. This visible‐frequency long‐focus system offers significant potential for noncontact nanoscale probing, integrated photonics, and optical interconnects. The proposed heterostructure engineering approach provides a versatile design paradigm for coupling hyperbolic polaritons with multiple plasmonic excitations, paving the way for advanced photonic applications.

title: Orthogonal Passivation of Polar Facets for Efficient InSb Quantum Dot SWIR Photodetectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) offer a heavy‐metal‐free route to short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetection, but their performance still lags behind lead‐ and mercury‐based CQD systems, and the surface chemistry that limits their performance is not well understood. Here, we identify two independent oxide‐derived trap pathways on the polar terminations of zincblende InSb: oxidation of the In‐terminated {111}A and Sb‐terminated {111}B facets creates chemically distinct mid‐gap states, each of which degrades carrier transport. Density functional theory calculations show that metal halides bind strongly to Sb‐terminated facets, but weakly to In‐terminated facets, while thiolates show the opposite preference; this asymmetry leaves single‐ligand passivation incomplete. Exploiting this orthogonality, we develop a facet‐specific exchange that passivates both terminations and removes their surface oxides in a single step. The resulting CQD films show a fivefold reduction in hole‐trap density and a sixfold improvement in hole mobility relative to thiol‐only controls. The photodetectors achieve 50% external quantum efficiency under 1 V reverse bias at 1390 nm, to the best of our knowledge, the highest reported for InSb CQD photodetectors in the 1300–1500 nm range, along with a 580 ns fall time and 95% photocurrent retention after 100 h of continuous operation.

title: Nanoscale Thermal Imaging of Dislocation‐Mediated Heat Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Dislocations are widely used to tailor lattice thermal conductivity in semiconductors and thermoelectrics, yet the local thermal resistance of individual buried dislocations and their spatial extent remain experimentally unresolved. Here, operando scanning transmission electron microscopy–electron energy‐loss spectroscopy thermometry, atomic‐resolution imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics are combined to map heat transport across a dislocation array within a 5°SrTiO 3 low‐angle grain boundary. The effective thermal conductance of the dislocation array is estimated to be ∼35.4 MW m − 2 K − 1 using the bulk reference conductivity, corresponding to a Kapitza length of ∼339 nm. Nanoscale temperature maps reveal a spatially heterogeneous resistance landscape: reconstructed dislocation cores act as sharp thermal bottlenecks over ∼2.14–5.17 nm, with steeper local temperature gradients than inter‐core regions, whereas inter‐core regions show weaker but more extended modulation over ∼8.34–11.57 nm. Correlative structural and vibrational analyses show that Ti─O bond distortion, Ti valence change, P4 optical‐phonon blueshift, and reduced local–bulk phonon density‐of‐states overlap create a core‐specific vibrational environment. These results uncover the underlying mechanism whereby atomic‐scale core reconstruction generates nanoscale localized thermal resistance, and offer quantitative descriptors for defect‐structure‐guided thermal design.

title: Transforming Pathological H 2 S Into a Photodynamic Amplifier: In Vivo Formation of Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 @Bi 2 S 3 Heterojunction for Microenvironment‐Adaptive Periodontitis Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Current periodontitis management is hindered by the inability to effectively reverse the dysbiotic microenvironment of persistent infection and restore immune homeostasis. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) presents a promising non‐invasive antibacterial strategy, its clinical efficacy remains limited by poor microenvironmental selectivity and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Herein, we engineer a microenvironment‐responsive “trash‐to‐treasure” PDT strategy based on Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 nanosheet‐assembled microspheres. This platform actively scavenges excess hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) within the periodontal pocket, triggering an in situ transformation into Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 @Bi 2 S 3 heterojunctions. This H 2 S‐triggered conversion neutralizes the pro‐inflammatory gasotransmitter and establishes an S‐scheme heterojunction with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The resulting reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative stress, together with targeted disruption of bacterial iron metabolism, enables highly efficient photodynamic eradication of major periodontopathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis . Moreover, Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 ‐mediated scavenging of pathological H 2 S alleviates inflammatory responses in human gingival fibroblasts and reactivates macrophage respiratory burst for intracellular bacterial clearance. In vivo evaluations in a rat periodontitis model demonstrate effective inflammation resolution, suppression of alveolar bone loss, and robust tissue regeneration. This work introduces an intelligent therapeutic strategy that hijacks pathological H 2 S as a photodynamic amplifier, establishing a microenvironment‐adaptive PDT paradigm for periodontal infection.

title: Unlocking the Potential of Magnesium‐Based Hydrogen Storage Composites via Advanced Thermodynamic and Kinetic Tuning Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient and safe solid‐state hydrogen storage technologies is pivotal for the transition toward sustainable clean energy. Magnesium is a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high gravimetric (7.6 wt.% for MgH 2 ) and volumetric storage capacity (110 kg m −3 ), abundance, and excellent reversibility. However, the practical application of Mg‐based materials is hindered by their high thermodynamic stability (ΔH = −74.7 kJ mol −1 H 2 ) and sluggish sorption kinetics. Here, we overview the latest advances in Mg‐based composites for high hydrogen storage performance. We discuss key material modification strategies, including catalysis, nanostructuring, alloying, and external field assistance to tune the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of Mg‐based materials. We stress the emerging role of machine learning in accelerating material design, performance prediction, and optimization. We also critically assess the techno‐economic viability of Mg‐based hydrogen storage within integrated hydrogen value chains. This assessment considers how storage connects with hydrogen production, transport, and end‐use applications. Finally, we outline challenges and future research directions, aiming to guide the rational design of next‐generation Mg‐based hydrogen storage materials and systems toward commercial applications.

title: Hoxa10 governs lifelong skeletal stem cell maintenance and bone repair
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) sustain bone homeostasis and regeneration throughout life, yet the transcriptional programs that preserve their identity remain poorly defined. Here we identify the distal Hox gene
                    Hoxa10
                    as a cell-autonomous regulator of skeletal stem cell maintenance. Using inducible genetic deletion, lineage tracing, single-cell transcriptomics, and injury models, we show that loss of
                    Hoxa10
                    leads to progressive depletion of SSPCs, impaired bone regeneration, and defective matrix organization. Mechanistically,
                    Hoxa10
                    maintains the undifferentiated state of skeletal stem cells by restraining premature osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic commitment, while promoting collagen III production and collagen fiber alignment within regenerative niches.
                    Hoxa10
                    -dependent regulation of extracellular matrix composition is restricted to primitive progenitors and is uncoupled from osteoblast differentiation. Notably, transient depletion of distal Hox genes in primary human SSPCs recapitulates the murine defects in proliferation, self-renewal, and differentiation restraint. Together, these findings define a conserved Hox-dependent program that preserves skeletal stem cell identity and regenerative competence, revealing how developmental transcription factors are repurposed to sustain the adult skeleton across the life span.

title: Ultrasound neural interface enabling acute spinal cord monitoring and blood flow modulation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. After wound closure, clinicians lack on-demand access to local spinal cord morphology and hemodynamics, and care therefore remains guided largely by systemic surrogates rather than direct postoperative insight into the injured cord. We present the Multimodal Ultrasound System for Injury Care (MUSIC), a temporary epidural ultrasound neural interface placed during standard decompression surgery to enable postoperative brightness-mode imaging, Doppler-derived hemodynamic monitoring, and future device-integrated ultrasound actuation. Across simulations, benchtop, human cadaveric, and porcine studies, MUSIC enabled on-demand visualization of cord structure, hematoma tracking, detection and longitudinal tracking of localized Doppler flow signatures attributable to the sulcal artery region, and, in healthy pigs, proof-of-concept focused ultrasound modulation of blood-flow velocity. MUSIC establishes a temporary postoperative acoustic interface that provides spinal cord information to inform monitoring, future management, and localized intervention strategies after SCI.

title: Self-charged toothbrush facilitates tooth healthcare maintenance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date. Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality, synergizing both optimal mechanical properties and stable electrical activity. The self-charged toothbrushes can generate reactive oxygen species to disrupt bacterial membrane integrity and diminish bacterial adhesion by combining static antibacterial inhibition through surface potential with dynamic piezoelectric stimulation. Clinical evaluation revealed that the localized piezoelectric stimulation of self-charged toothbrushes can mitigate plaque formation and gingival inflammation. Mechanistic studies further revealed that the self-charged toothbrushes induced oxidative damage to the oral pathogenic bacterial membranes, thereby impairing the ATP-binding cassette transporter pathway. Hence, this study developed a concept of piezoelectric PVDF toothbrushes that combine physical cleaning with sustained antibacterial effect, thus highlighting the potential of self-charged materials in advancing oral healthcare.

title: Genetic dissection of cell type–specific congenital heart disease variants reveals ETS1 control of vascular smooth muscle cell fate
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Numerous congenital heart disease (CHD) risk variants lie in cis-regulatory elements, yet the impact of variants in repressed and bivalent chromatin on cell type–specific heart development is unclear. Here, we generated a single-cell multiomic atlas of human cardiac differentiation by jointly profiling H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and transcriptomes in individual cells, classifying cis-regulatory elements into six chromatin states, enabling prioritization of 610 CHD-associated noncoding variants enriched in lineage- and state-specific regulatory elements, including repressive and bivalent regions. CRISPR knockin of selected variants perturbed nearby gene expression and impaired cardiac differentiation. Dissection of a Polycomb-marked variant near
                    ETS1
                    (ETS proto-oncogene 1) revealed local H3K27me3 loss, H3K27ac gain, and ETS1 up-regulation, which redirects differentiation toward second-heart-field progenitors with epithelial characteristics at early stages and, ultimately, highly migratory
                    ETS1
                    +
                    vascular smooth muscle cells. Together, our work establishes a single-cell chromatin-state framework for interpreting noncoding CHD risk variants and uncovers an ETS1-driven program linking Polycomb-deregulated noncoding variation to aberrant vascular smooth muscle fate commitment during human cardiogenesis.

title: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Spin-polarized lasers hold great potential in integrated photonic devices for secure communication, optical interconnections, and advanced optical devices, offering excellent properties superior to those of conventional lasers. Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites are promising candidates for spin-polarized lasers, because their potential structural inversion asymmetry will result in strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) facilitating spin injection and hence spin splitting of electronic bands. However, strong SOC involves a trade-off between spin injection and spin lifetimes. How to prolong spin lifetimes in the lasing regime while maintaining the optical gain make it challenging to sustain spin polarization for lasing. Here, we unveil the underlying spin mechanism and successfully realize quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing by suppressing fast spin relaxation through triplet exciton regulation using organic cations of phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). We identify the Bir-Aronov-Pikus (BAP) mechanism is the dominant spin relaxation mechanism preventing the achievement of spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites. By modulating the reverse intersystem crossing of triplet excitons, the D’yakonov-Perel’ (DP) mechanism becomes to play a key role and results in a new-emerged prolonged spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, which is ∼5 times that of the BAP-induced one. Consequently, spin-polarized lasing is realized below 200 K, and the threshold is 30.2% lower than that for linearly polarized excitation. This work underscores the potential of PEA-based quasi-2D perovskites in spin-polarized lasing and contributes to the rapid advancements in perovskite spintronic devices.

title: Engineered synbiotic microspheres enable system-level reprogramming of the gut-immune-vascular axis in chronic inflammatory vascular disease
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders sustained by maladaptive cross-organ immunometabolic coupling, yet current therapeutic strategies remain largely lesion-centered and fail to address upstream drivers of disease persistence. Here, we identify the gut-immune-vascular axis as a system-level pathogenic unit that integrates gut microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and vascular immune activation into a self-reinforcing pathological circuit. Through integrated clinical profiling and cross-species validation, we demonstrate that disruption of this axis is characterized by coordinated probiotic depletion, expansion of proinflammatory taxa, translocation of microbial endotoxins, accumulation of microbiota-derived metabolites, and macrophage polarization toward a proinflammatory phenotype along the gut-vascular continuum. To therapeutically target this axis, we engineer enzyme-responsive synbiotic microspheres that codeliver probiotics, a microbial metabolic pathway inhibitor, and a prebiotic within a protective polymeric matrix, enabling site-specific intestinal activation and coordinated microbiota-metabolic modulation. This engineered system restores intestinal barrier integrity, reprograms microbial ecology and metabolite output, suppresses immunometabolic dysfunction, and robustly attenuates pathological vascular remodeling across cellular, murine, and large-animal models, with in-stent restenosis serving as a representative disease context. Collectively, this work establishes axis-oriented immunometabolic reprogramming as a generalizable therapeutic paradigm and highlights engineered synbiotic platforms as scalable tools for system-level intervention in chronic inflammatory diseases.

title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in mitochondrial and ribosomal genes are observed in all different cell types. In addition, hibernation triggers an inflammatory-like response in microglia that in part resembles cell states observed in Alzheimer’s disease, but here in the absence of Aβ-accumulation and neurodegeneration. These findings reveal brain transformations that might help preserve vital functions under extreme conditions and they suggest that early cellular changes in AD may be a natural adaptive process.

title: BCLAF1 links RNA splicing to ATF4-dependent metabolic adaptation in acute myeloid leukemia
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Clinically derived micro- and nanoplastic uptake drives spatiotemporally confined metabolic stress revealed by bond-selective imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. Here, we use chemical bond–selective stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy and cell models that decouple continuous exposure from intracellular retention to directly visualize clinically derived MP/NP-cell interactions. Cellular stress occurs primarily during MP/NP exposure, accompanied by alterations in lipid droplet (LD) composition. In contrast, following extracellular removal, intracellularly retained MP/NP become largely inert, with recovery of lipid metabolism and cellular functions. Lipidomics identifies arachidonic acid (AA) as a key dysregulated metabolite, and SRS imaging further reveals transient, spatially confined AA enrichment in MP/NP–proximal LDs during uptake. Phospholipid coating of MP/NP attenuates LD alterations and cytotoxicity while preserving particle internalization, establishing uptake-driven metabolic stress, rather than long-term intracellular retention, as a primary source of MP/NP–induced damage.

title: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, involves progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. Early detection of this neurodegeneration is critical, yet current clinical methods often identify disease only after substantial damage has occurred. This preliminary study used high-resolution adaptive optics–optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to track individual retinal ganglion cells in patients and healthy volunteers over 3 to 5 years. Results revealed higher neurodegeneration in glaucoma compared to normal aging. We observed 4.16 to 6.86% annual decrease in cell density in glaucoma, far exceeding the 0.27% cell loss rate observed in the healthy volunteer group. Critically, AO-OCT detected progression significantly earlier, identifying cell loss 0.74 years before conventional OCT and 1.49 years before visual field testing. These findings demonstrate AO-OCT as a more sensitive tool capable of monitoring glaucomatous damage with superior precision, potentially representing a major advancement over current clinical imaging.

title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major uncertainty in projections of future climate. However, direct evidence for AMOC tipping behavior on orbital timescales remains scarce. Here, we reconstruct the strength of Iceland-Scotland Overflow Water, a key lower branch of the deep Atlantic circulation, over the past 800,000 years by combining 12 current-speed records from North Atlantic sediment cores with a data-driven hybrid model. The resulting reconstruction reveals persistent alternation between weak (glacial) and strong (interglacial) circulation modes, pervasive millennial-scale variability within both regimes, and systematic asymmetry between weak-to-strong recoveries and strong-to-weak collapses. Threshold and phase-space analyses show that regime shifts occur within a narrow window of atmospheric carbon dioxide and sea level and often follow hysteresis-like loops. Although bistability persists throughout the last 800,000 years, its sensitivity and timing evolve through time. These findings provide long-term, high-resolution, data-driven constraints on the bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters and its implications for AMOC resilience in a warming world.

title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor–family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.

title: A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease progression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Identifying the neurobiological basis of cognitive vulnerability is essential for preventing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We derived the Alzheimer’s Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome (ARC) by contrasting SuperAgers (SA), an extreme phenotype of preserved late-life memory, with AD using resting-state fMRI. ARC distinguished SA from AD in a discovery cohort (
                    N
                     = 290; AUC = 0.85) and replicated independently (
                    N
                     = 143), involving prefrontal, temporal, and insular networks and associating with brain age. Applied to cognitively unimpaired adults (discovery:
                    N
                     = 818; replication:
                    N
                     = 497), ARC-based subtyping revealed SA-like and AD-like subgroups with comparable baseline cognition but divergent longitudinal trajectories. AD-like individuals exhibited faster cognitive decline, greater amyloid-β accumulation, and higher AD conversion risk. Exploratory GWAS nominated
                    CLYBL
                    and
                    FRMD6
                    as candidate novel loci associated with the subtype difference. These findings suggest that ARC captures a continuous connectomic dimension of cognitive aging spanning SA, cognitively typical aging, and AD, highlighting the potential of functional connectomic variation for early risk stratification in AD.

title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence, whereas others showed deterministic shifts in symbiont community composition. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, consistent with deterministic adaptation to moderate thermal stress but stochastic accumulation of diversity under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host-microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change.

title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the
                    N
                    6
                    -methyladenosine (m
                    6
                    A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m
                    6
                    A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m
                    6
                    A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mars is reputed to lack ongoing volcanic activity. However, marsquakes were revealed recently, and clues to volcanism younger than tens of million years have accumulated. While sulfur dioxide, so far undetected, could testify to ongoing eruptive activity, evidence of active magma chambers may be better identified by seepage of halogen gases, such as hydrogen chloride (HCl). Observations by Atmospheric Chemistry Suite led to the widespread observations of HCl at part-per-billion levels in the atmosphere of Mars during the warm perihelion period, attributed to aerosol-atmospheric sources. Here, we report HCl detections during the cold aphelion season that are isolated in the Alba Mons region. We also identify fresh and narrow (<1 meter) fissures in this area, which we interpret to be potential HCl pathways rooted into magmatic bodies at depth. Our results are best explained by ongoing igneous processes in the Martian interior.

title: Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, stratigraphic integrity, and confirming early inland dispersal: Evaluating peopling of the Americas modeling
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Statistical models shape debates over the timing and geography of the initial peopling of the Americas, but their value depends on testing their assumptions against archaeological evidence. We examine the Apparent Stratigraphic Integrity Index (ASI), used to infer postdepositional mixing at Late Pleistocene sites and support a relatively late occupation of temperate North America. ASI describes vertical discontinuity in binned artifact-frequency profiles; it does not directly measure artifact movement or stratigraphic integrity. At Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, Idaho, the 5-centimeter absolute-elevation bins used to calculate ASI do not reflect the actual stratigraphic positions of artifacts across the irregular LU2 surface on which LU3 loess accumulated. The resulting ASI value cannot support claims of large-scale vertical mixing. Independent chronological, stratigraphic, pedogenic, archaeological, and excavation evidence supports the integrity of the ∼16,000–calibrated-years-before-the-present occupation. Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe provides early inland evidence expected under coastal-migration models, showing that models should be evaluated against archaeological evidence rather than used to override it.

title: Oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography for sub–100-μm zirconia dental veneers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: High-resolution vat photopolymerization of ceramics is constrained by light scattering, which broadens cured features, and by shallow penetration, which limits interlayer bonding. This trade-off is particularly damaging for microscale structures such as no-preparation dental veneers. We introduce an oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography strategy in which an oxygen-permeable release film creates an interfacial inhibition field in high-solid–loading zirconia slurry. Rather than uniformly reducing curing, oxygen preferentially filters low-dose scattered light at pattern edges while preserving curing in the projected core. This anisotropic inhibition reshapes the accuracy-depth trade-off, enabling optimized multilayer printing of thin-wall zirconia. The process enabled reproducible fabrication of ∼80-micrometer zirconia veneers with high trueness, improved marginal adaptation, and handling-related strength comparable to substantially thicker milled veneers. The approach provides the potential for minimally invasive dental restoration and a general strategy for high-resolution additive manufacturing of strongly scattering ceramic suspensions.

title: N6-methyladenosine–dependent ARv7 translation couples lactate metabolism with enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Enzalutamide (Enz)–resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as an
                    N
                    6-methyladenosine (m
                    6
                    A)–modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m
                    6
                    A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m
                    6
                    A-dependent translational regulation.

title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8+ T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)–high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-I
                    high
                    contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8
                    +
                    T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor– and chimeric antigen receptor–based immunotherapies in IFN-I
                    high
                    tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-I
                    high
                    / IFNAR1
                    low
                    axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Independent origin of genomic imprinting in placental fish
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Genomic imprinting results in biased expression of one parental allele. Such non-Mendelian expression occurs in angiosperms and placental mammals, which share having an active paternal genome during maternal offspring provisioning. It is hypothesized that imprinting modulates conflict between maternal control of resource allocation and paternal control of resource acquisition. If true, then imprinting should evolve in any organism that evolves a placenta. Here, we demonstrate genomic imprinting in a placental poeciliid fish,
                    Poeciliopsis prolifica
                    . Using transcriptomes from reciprocal crosses between two inbred strains, we identified 84 protein-coding genes with robust evidence of imprinting in
                    P. prolifica
                    placenta. These include the teleost ortholog of mammalian imprinted gene,
                    grb10
                    , and a pair of adjacent genes,
                    dpp4
                    and
                    gcga
                    , with opposing effects on glucose metabolism that are oppositely imprinted in a fashion that potentially resolves parental conflict. Significantly elevated allelic DNA methylation on the promoters of two focal imprinted genes suggests epigenetic mechanisms of imprinting similar to those in mammals. We also discovered the convergent recruitment of a gene network associated with nutrient transport in mammals. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of genomic imprinting in a non-mammalian vertebrate and supports the potential role of imprinting in resolving parental conflict.

title: Amphipathic helices repurpose a Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter to function at Plasmodium–erythrocyte membrane contact sites
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The interface between the malaria parasite
                    Plasmodium spp.
                    and its host erythrocyte critically mediates nutrient uptake, lipid exchange, and protein export required for parasite replication and thus pathogenesis. Approximately half of this interface consists of narrow membrane contact sites, a region defined by only 3 to 4 nm of aqueous space between the parasite plasma membrane and the parasitophorous vacuole membrane. Despite its extent, the region remains largely uncharacterized and inaccessible, not least due to its narrowness. The sole identified resident is the
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    Niemann-Pick Type C1-Related protein, PfNCR1, an essential Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter, suggesting this conserved transporter family has evolved an unconventional adaptation for localizing to membrane contact sites that can reveal a mechanism to access the region. Here, using live-cell microscopy and assessment of cholesterol homeostasis, we identify a helix–linker–helix (HLH) domain as the necessary modification for efficient PfNCR1 localization. We find that correct localization is required for the parasite to maintain low cholesterol levels, connecting targeting to function. Using a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored fluorescent reporter as a minimal membrane-associated protein, we show that the HLH domain is sufficient to drive localization to the narrow membrane contact site region. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that targeting depends on the physicochemical character of the targeting domain rather than a specific primary sequence, identifying amphipathicity as a determining property of the HLH domain. Taken together, we propose physicochemical partitioning as a fundamental principle for protein targeting at the
                    Plasmodium
                    –erythrocyte interface, and for driving direct functional interactions of a Patched/NPC1-like protein with a second membrane.

title: Defining epidemiologically relevant units of cholera transmission in sub-Saharan Africa
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Much remains unknown about cholera transmission dynamics in Africa. Applying both traditional phylogeographic techniques and innovative methods for combining epidemiologic and genomic data, we identified three to four distinct “cholera transmission units” within which cross-border cholera transmission has been more frequent. These units can be grouped into two major transmission clusters, one in Western Africa and bordering countries and one spanning the Central, Eastern, and Southern regions. Simulation studies show that these clusters can be used to assess the risk of international spread of introduced cholera strains and identify heterogeneities in the speed of international spread based on outbreak location. Our methods further allow us to infer cholera incidence attributable to specific lineages in the absence of sequencing data. This work has clear implications for cholera control.

title: Accumulated radicals by GHz femtosecond burst drive one-step superhydrophobic conversion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Short-lived radicals usually decay before they can drive long-range reactions, making laser-induced radical chain reactions difficult to sustain. Here, we used GHz femtosecond bursts to temporally couple excitation events, allowing reactive intermediates from preceding subpulses to remain available for subsequent reactions and favoring their transient accumulation relative to isolated-pulse excitation. Consistent with this temporally coupled process, the methylphenyl silicone resin/graphene/CuFe
                    2
                    O
                    4
                    /SiO
                    2
                    composite coating exhibits a threshold-like nonlinear wettability transition near 430 subpulses. Compared with the microsecond-spaced single-pulse femtosecond regime, the sub-nanosecond GHz burst produces more extensive chemical conversion, enabling one-step bond reorganization and phase transformation and yielding a low-adhesion superhydrophobic surface with a contact angle of 161° ± 0.7° without posttreatment. Pulse-timing–controlled radical-mediated chemistry thus provides a time-domain strategy for ultrafast materials synthesis.

title: Oxygen fugacity, temperature, and pressure of Siberian eclogitic diamonds: Implications for the Archaean convecting mantle redox state
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
