title: Relay Catalysis on Phase‐Separated Janus–CuCo Alloys for Efficient Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction at Industrial Low Concentration
abstract: ABSTRACT Earth‐abundant Cu and Co are attractive electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO 3 − RR); however, conventional solid‐solution alloys with single‐phase active sites lack effective intermediate spillover, impeding the hydrogenation of multiple reaction intermediates and limiting NH 3 selectivity under dilute nitrate conditions. Here we report phase‐separated yet electronically coupled Janus–CuCo alloys synthesized via a time–charge regulated electrochemical reduction strategy, forming metallic Cu/Co domains with a well‐defined interphase electronic structure. This Janus architecture enables relay catalysis, in which Cu domains activate NO 3 − , intermediates migrate to Cu−Co interfaces for hydrogenation, and adjacent Co domains promote subsequent NH 3 formation. In situ characterizations reveal pronounced Cu–Co synergy, where Co sites regulate *H‐mediated hydrogenation while the balanced surface coverage of *H and *NO 3 − optimizes NH 3 selectivity and yield. Consequently, the optimized Janus Cu−Co catalyst, Janus–Cu 70 Co 30 /NOMC, achieves a peak NH 3 Faradaic efficiency (FE NH3 ) of 95.5% at −500 mA cm −2 and delivers a FE NH3 of 93.1% with an NH 3 yield rate of 4.2 mg h −1 mg cat −1 at −0.4 V vs RHE in an MEA flow cell under low nitrate concentrations. These findings establish phase separation with electronic coupling, enabled by electrochemical time–charge control, as an effective design principle for efficient multistep NO 3 − RR electrocatalysis.

title: Decoupling Oxygen Reduction From Hydrogen Oxidation on Platinum via Phosphorus Coordination for Reversal‐Tolerant and Durable PEM Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT During the start‐up/shut‐down (SU/SD) processes of proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low‐loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P‐BP catalyst. The P‐coordination downshifts the d ‐band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR‑FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P‐BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P‐BP achieves a 10.8‐fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P‐BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design for electrocatalysts.

title: Atmosphere‐Dependent Encapsulation and Dewetting in Au/ZnO: A Transient‐Overlayer Strategy for Maximizing Metal‐Support Interfacial Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) has traditionally been viewed as a static phenomenon that modulates catalysis through site blocking. Here, we challenge this classical view by demonstrating that SMSI in Au/ZnO is an atmosphere‐dependent dynamic process that can be harnessed to engineer catalytic interfaces. Using in situ transmission electron microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we track the structural evolution of the Au/ZnO interface throughout redox cycles and reaction conditions. Under H 2 , oxygen vacancy formation triggers ZnO x encapsulation, followed by AuZn alloying at elevated temperature, which induces nanoparticle reconstruction and expands the metal‐support interfacial area. Upon exposure to O 2 , the alloy decomposes, and the ZnO x overlayer dewets into nanoislands, with some regions undergoing complete retraction. Under CO oxidation conditions, the fully encapsulated state is lost, yet the H 2 ‐pretreated catalyst exhibits superior activity and stability. This enhancement arises from alloying‐induced interface reconstruction together with residual ZnO nanoislands that persist after dewetting, creating an enlarged and highly active metal–oxide interface. Our work demonstrates a transient‐overlayer strategy for catalyst design, in which a pre‐formed SMSI layer serves as a precursor that, through controlled redox cycling or reaction conditions, transforms into a high‐interface area, sintering‐resistant catalytic architecture, thereby transcending the classical encapsulation‐activity dilemma.

title: Structure‐Guided Design of Pepper‐Binding Fluorophores Through Hydrogen‐Bonding Engineering
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Pepper fluorescent RNAs (FRs) enable spatiotemporal imaging of intracellular RNA with high resolution. Although spectral optimization of the HBC scaffold has extended coverage from cyan to red, systematic refinement of binding affinity, photostability, and brightness remains largely unexplored. We describe a hydrogen‐bonding strategy that strengthens fluorophore‐aptamer interactions by incorporating hydroxyl groups or polyethylene glycol (PEG) moieties into HBC derivatives. The resulting compounds, MBC and PBC620, bind Pepper over 6‐fold and 10‐fold more tightly than their parent dyes HBC and HBC620, respectively, and exhibit correspondingly higher signal‐to‐noise ratios and enhanced photostability, with 2.1‐fold and 1.5‐fold increases in cellular brightness. Molecular models reveal that improved affinity stems from optimally positioned hydrogen bonds with RNA nucleotides. MBC enables real‐time tracking of genomic loci with enhanced contrast compared to standard HBC. This work establishes structure‐guided interface engineering as a general strategy for improving fluorescent RNA systems.

title: Resurrecting Robust CYP152 Peroxygenases for Versatile Biocatalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Cytochrome P450 CYP152s are attractive biocatalysts which catalyze decarboxylation and hydroxylation of fatty acids using H 2 O 2 as a co‐substrate (peroxygenase activity). Contemporary CYP152s have limited stability and substrate scope. Here we characterized eight reconstructed variants of CYP152 obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The results showed that variants remote from Jeotgalicoccus sp. 8456 (CYP152L1) in the tree used for the ASR tended to catalyze hydroxylation, while nodes closer to CYP152L1 favored decarboxylation; this transition correlates with Q85H substitution and FG‐loop insertion alongside other structural features. Three reconstructed variants exhibit high T m (66°C–76°C), tolerance to solvents, H 2 O 2 , extreme pH, and use non‐native substrates. CYP152‐AncG2 can catalyze one‐pot chemoenzymatic C─C bond coupling reactions to synthesize methoxy stilbene and can serve as a template for directed evolution. X‐ray structure at 1.83 Å and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations indicate that loop structures, surface salt bridges, and optimized access tunnels in CYP152‐AncG2 are key for enabling its superior features. These findings provide insights into the structural and evolutionary features of robust peroxygenase templates for expanding peroxygenase biocatalysis.

title: Security-oriented optimization method for enhancing resilient operation of urban integrated energy cyber-physical system
Aniline–Peroxide-Initiated Cyclodextrin-Containing Monoliths for Scalable PFAS Removal from Water
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are a class of persistent environmental contaminants that cause negative health effects. These health concerns and impending regulations motivate demand for PFAS removal technologies. Such technologies must be capable of high-throughput, continuous-flow operation, and maintaining treatment performance at large-scales in municipal and industrial treatment systems. Many PFAS remediation technologies rely on particle-based sorbents, which are subject to mass-transfer limitations in large-scale flow-through systems that can limit PFAS removal performance. Recently, we introduced monolithic sorbents for PFAS removal based on styrene-functionalized β-cyclodextrin polymers whose porosity can reduce these mass-transfer limitations. The first monolith formulations were prepared by photoinitiating polymerization within flow-through columns, which limited the monolith’s practical scalability. Here, we address this limitation by using a redox initiation process at room temperature, which is compatible with the high internal phase emulsion and enables scalable fabrication across column dimensions. Mercury porosimetry revealed a bimodal pore size distribution and a larger characteristic maximum pore size in the redox-initiated monoliths compared to the monomodal pore size distribution observed in the photoinitiated materials. Chemical composition and batch adsorption performance remained consistent across redox-initiated monoliths scaled to 36 times the original monolith cross-sectional area. Redox-initiated monoliths outperformed photoinitiated monoliths in flow-through columns, showing later breakthrough of the short-chain PFAS, perfluorobutanoic acid. We also evaluated the PFAS removal performance of scaled redox-initiated monoliths in columns of increasing diameters (0.5, 1, and 1.5 cm). Their performance was consistent across scales, indicating that redox-initiated monoliths with larger cross-sectional areas maintain their promising sorption performance.

title: Simultaneously Boosting Stability and High-Temperature Performance of Ni-Rich Cathode Materials by a Negative-Thermal-Expansion Fast Ion Conductor
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nickel-rich layered oxide cathodes have attracted extensive attention for high-energy batteries due to their high capacity, but face challenges such as structural instability, mechanical degradation, interfacial side reactions, and thermal runaway. To address these issues, a multiple-benefit strategy is proposed to modify LiNi0.92Co0.03Mn0.05O2 (NCM92) using Li1.1La0.1Zr1.9(PO4)3 (LLZP) featuring both high ionic conductivity and negative thermal expansion through a facile way. The NCM92 modified with 3 wt % LLZP (denoted as LLZP3) exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Compared to pristine NCM92, the Li+ diffusion coefficient and the discharge specific capacity at 10 C are, respectively, increased by 94.2 and 19.9%, while the capacity retention ratios are, respectively, enhanced by 26.0 and 23.4 percentage points after 200 cycles at 25 °C and 60 °C. Meanwhile, the strain after cycling at 60 °C and the released heat when first charged to 4.3 V are reduced by 55.6% and 62.4%, respectively. According to multifarious characterizations, LLZP can significantly improve the Li+ diffusion kinetics of NCM92, alleviate released heat and volume expansion, and suppress microcrack formation and side reactions during charge/discharge cycling. Noticeably, LLZP exhibits anisotropic volumetric contraction via in situ absorbing heat to enhance thermal safety and interfacial stability. It provides a universal and practical approach for developing high-performance energy materials.

title: Drop-to-Drop Transfer of Magnetic Activity: Imparting Significant Heterogeneity and Reactivity to a Drop via Functionality Transfer from Another Drop
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interactions between nanoparticles (NPs) and liquid drops have been widely utilized to manipulate both drops and NPs. However, achieving their separation without altering the intrinsic state of either component has remained a significant challenge in NP-laden drop systems. In our previous work (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2024, 16, 64253–64263), we addressed this challenge by extracting magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) from the interior of an MNP-laden drop as a compact aggregate under the influence of an external magnetic field. In the present paper, we develop a technique that enables the seamless transfer of this extracted MNP aggregate from one liquid drop (the source drop) into the interior of a second liquid drop (the receiver drop). Remarkably, the aggregate, which can be tracked throughout the transfer process, is transferred nearly in its entirety, while neither drop undergoes any permanent deformation throughout the process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a seamless drop-to-drop transfer of NPs, or, more broadly, the transfer of one drop’s functionality to another (here magnetic activity) without permanently altering the morphology of either drop. Beyond facilitating the NP transfer, the process transforms the receiver drop into a heterogeneous system that exhibits a variety of intriguing phenomena. For example, the transferred NPs can self-assemble into either skyscraper-like solid structures or magnetically responsive liquid layers. The nature of these assemblies depends on whether the MNP transfer occurs once or multiple times, and these assemblies display markedly different dynamics when subjected to magnetic fields of varying orientations, as well as oscillating and rotating magnetic fields. Furthermore, the transfer process converts the receiver drop into a highly stable microreactor for chemical reactions, enabling reaction products to form and persist while remaining minimally exposed to external disturbances that could otherwise compromise their stability.

title: Defect Passivation via a Bifunctional Guanidinium Sulfamate Ligand for High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving high crystallinity and low defect density remains a critical bottleneck for maximizing the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, we introduce guanidinium sulfamate (GASM) as a bifunctional ligand to modulate the defect chemistry of perovskite films. DFT calculations reveal thermodynamically favorable binding of GASM to defect sites on selected α-FAPbI3 (100) surface models. Separately, the stronger (100) diffraction response observed by XRD is consistent with improved film crystallinity, although a change in out-of-plane texture cannot be excluded. Meanwhile, theoretical and spectroscopic results suggest Pb–O coordination involving the sulfamate moiety and N–H···I hydrogen bonding involving the guanidinium moiety, consistent with the observed defect-passivation effect. The GASM-treated perovskite films show a stronger (100) diffraction response, larger grains, and a longer photoluminescence lifetime. The resulting n–i–p structured PSCs deliver a champion PCE of 24.43%, alongside environmental stability. These results highlight the potential of GASM as an additive for improving perovskite film quality and suppressing defect-assisted nonradiative recombination, contributing to enhanced photovoltaic performance.

title: Open-Air Fabricated Pseudo-Planar Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells with Improved Efficiency and Thermostability via Suppression of Interfacial Degradation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Boosting both photovoltaic performance and long-term stability is currently the main challenge for organic solar cells (OSCs). In this regard, adopting a pseudo-planar heterojunction (PPHJ) photoactive layer is a promising solution because of its favorable vertical phase distribution; however, it is subject to the limitation of donor/acceptor (D/A) interfacial degradation. Herein, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is introduced as a multifunctional donor additive, enabling the suppression of interface degradation in the PPHJ photoactive layer and thereby improving the efficiency and thermostability of devices. Specifically, the introduction of PVDF slightly enhances the molecular packing and dielectric property of the photoactive layer, leading to reduced exciton binding energy (Eb) and enhanced charge transport capability of the materials. These improvements stabilize the interfacial morphology and thus suppress interfacial degradation, including deposition-induced and aging-induced degradation. Moreover, PVDF’s hydrophobicity improves moisture tolerance, enabling reliable open-air fabrication of the photoactive layer under high humidity. As a result, the open-air fabricated OSCs achieve an impressive efficiency of 19.24% with enhanced storage stability and thermal stability, which is one of the highest efficiencies for open-air fabricated OSCs. This work highlights the importance of suppressing interfacial degradation in improving performance and stability of PPHJ OSCs and provides a promising strategy to address it.

title: Carboxylic Acid-Based Hole Transport Layer with Both Anchoring and Passivation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The hole transport layer (HTL) plays a pivotal role in the performance of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), especially in carrier transport, anchoring to the substrate as a buried interface, and defect passivation. Novel HTLs that simultaneously achieve indium tin oxide (ITO) substrate anchoring, passivation of buried perovskite defects, and favorable interfacial energy alignment are seldom addressed. In this work, we designed a novel HTL (denoted as TPCOOH), which is functionalized with dicarboxylic acid groups in the central phenyl ring, which can anchor onto ITO substrates and passivate the top perovskite, as well as coupling with methylthio-substituted triphenylamine and thiophene units to generate suitable energy alignment and transfer the hole, realizing both passivation and anchoring effects. TPHex, as a control, had dihexyl substitution in the center. Inverted PSC devices based on TPCOOH and TPHex as hole transport layers (0.1 cm2) achieved power conversion efficiencies of 24.68% and 23.72%, respectively. The improved efficiency of TPCOOH-based devices is attributed to suppressed nonradiative recombination, rapid interfacial charge transfer, and minimal energy loss due to well-matched energy levels. These improvements are ascribed to the carboxyl groups in TPCOOH, which anchor to ITO, thus ensuring better film coverage and improved charge transport, while the passivation functionality simultaneously mitigates perovskite defects. Notably, the TPCOOH and TPHex devices retain 75% and 65% of their initial power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) after 1200 h of thermal aging at 65 ± 5 °C in a nitrogen atmosphere.

title: Compound effects of traffic and climate on electric vehicle HVAC energy consumption: a spatiotemporal framework with city-level attribution
abstract: Real-world electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption can deviate by 20-40% from rated values, driven by ambient temperature, traffic congestion, and route characteristics. Existing studies treat these factors in isolation or as static loads, leaving the compound effect of co-varying climate and traffic on HVAC energy unquantified and per-route attribution unavailable. We develop a spatiotemporal simulation framework that couples traffic-aware driving speed, time- and location-specific ambient temperature, and physics-based submodels (cabin HVAC, traction, battery thermal management) at the segment level, paired with a regression-based decomposition that attributes HVAC variability to temperature and trip-duration components on a per-route basis. Applied through a factorial design across seven UK cities and eight radial routes from Manchester, the framework shows total energy varying by 14\% across cities while HVAC energy varies by up to 89\%, making cabin thermal management the primary differentiator under winter conditions. Trip duration, set by traffic and road type, is frequently the dominant driver of HVAC variability: in London, 83\% of above-average HVAC energy is attributable to congestion-extended trip time rather than to temperature. The decomposition yields a closed-form HVAC model from three inputs (ambient temperature, average speed, trip distance), with physically interpretable coefficients and straightforward transfer to other vehicles or regions through three coefficient re-fits. EV range variability is substantially shaped by traffic and road-network characteristics, with implications for route planning, infrastructure design, and energy equity.

title: Quantifying Anion Selectivity in SEI Formation for Ether-Based Electrolytes in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract While current electrolyte design strategies for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) emphasize the importance of an anion-dominated Li+ solvation structure to promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), solvation structure-SEI composition relationships remain challenging to quantify. Here, we systematically investigate a series of ether/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl) imide (LiFSI) electrolytes and quantify the lithium fluoride formed from FSI– decomposition using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. We find that both an anion-dominated electrolyte solvation structure and a reductively stable solvent are necessary to achieve anion-selective SEI formation and establish a framework for anion selectivity in ether-LiFSI electrolytes, guided by density functional theory-derived solvent descriptors, which aligns with existing examples of ether-based Li metal electrolytes. Using this model, we identify an electrolyte formulation of tert-butyl methyl ether and tert-amyl methyl ether that achieves a Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%. Ultimately, this study establishes key electrolyte solvent-interphase-performance relationships to enable high-performance LMBs.

title: Low-Solvent Mechanochemical MOF Carrier Nanoarchitectonics for Targeted Quercetin Delivery for Dual-Mode ROS and Anti-inflammation Protection against LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nowadays, inhalable administration of nanomedicines is an appealing concept for acute lung injury (ALI). For ALI nanomedicine, it is appealing to achieve targeted delivery and on-demand release in the ALI microenvironment, which is acidic, rich in reactive oxygen species (ROS), and with elevated inflammatory mediator levels. Notably, customized metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) could fulfill these requirements and thus are promising nanocarriers for ALI medicine delivery, but MOFs formulated often suffer from unreacted residues with hazardous risk. Herein, we report a low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method to formulate cerium-doped zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (Ce-ZIFs) stabilized by Pluronic F127 as drug delivery nanocarriers to load quercetin for targeted preventive ALI therapy. The nanoplatform exhibits robust structural integrity, high drug loading capacity, excellent biocompatibility, and pH-responsive release of quercetin under acidic conditions, mimicking the inflamed lung microenvironment. Importantly, the nanoplatform ameliorates pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6), inhibits pulmonary edema, and attenuates alveolar injury in an LPS-induced ALI mouse model. Notably, Ce/ZIF promotes the Ce+3/Ce+4 redox process to generate catalase-like activity for catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and sustainable antioxidant properties. Transcriptome sequencing and biological validation also revealed that the nanoplatform showed its remarkable ability to counteract LPS-induced oxidative damage and inflammatory responses by suppressing Th1 cell polarization. This work demonstrates a Ce/ZIF platform formulated using a scalable, low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method, presenting a biocompatible MOF platform with significant promise for targeted pulmonary delivery with protective potential against LPS-induced acute lung injury.

title: Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local electrostatic functionality and probing confined-liquid dielectric physics in two-dimensional (2D) material assemblies.

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma–Enabled SiO x Nanocoatings for Surface Energy Modulation and Enhanced Seed Germination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Modern agricultural systems demand higher and more reliable yields under increasing constraints on land, water, and fertilizer inputs. Rapid and uniform seed germination is therefore critical for improving crop establishment and overall yield performance. Although existing strategies, such as ionizing gas treatments, polymer coatings, and nanoparticle-based seed treatments, can enhance water uptake and early vigor, they often suffer from limited stability, processing complexity, or potential seed damage. Here, we introduce a dry, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP)-assisted deposition platform for the conformal SiOx nanocoating of seeds, enabling a hydrophilic, storage-stable surface modification under ambient conditions. The deposition process was systematically optimized to achieve rapid, uniform coating formation directly on the seed surface. As a model system, corn seeds (Zea mays L.) were coated with SiOx nanofilms under optimized conditions. Wettability analysis revealed a ∼4-fold reduction in the static water contact angle for SiOx-coated seeds relative to pristine controls, compared with a ∼2.9-fold reduction for plasma-treated seeds without precursor introduction. Importantly, the SiOx-induced hydrophilicity exhibited superior stability, showing less than 3° contact angle recovery after 21 days of storage, whereas plasma-treated seeds alone displayed ∼50° recovery within 120 h. This stable and enhanced surface hydrophilicity translated into accelerated germination and improved early seedling vigor, resulting in SiOx-coated seeds exhibiting improved total seedling growth immediately after treatment and maintaining an approximately 38% increase compared with pristine controls after storage, demonstrating consistent storage stability. In comparison, the early-germination and seedling-growth advantages of plasma-treated seeds diminished substantially after storage, indicating that CAP-deposited SiOx provides a more persistent and storage-stable functional modification. Collectively, these results establish CAP-deposited SiOx nanocoatings as a scalable, solvent-free nanotechnology platform for stabilizing seed hydrophilicity, accelerating germination, and promoting early seedling growth under agronomically relevant conditions.

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology
abstract: Predictive human-relevant model systems are outlined in a Review by integrating engineered materials and microenvironments, human tissue and organ models, computational approaches, and closed-loop strategies. Controlling the boundary conditions, biological organization, measurements and model calibration can improve mechanistic insight, reproducibility and translational relevance across applications.

title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks
abstract: Adapt-ring networks consisting of dense, reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains and sparsely crosslinked polyethylene glycol form adaptive polymer materials that remodel and strengthen in response to mechanical stress.

title: Co-generation of energy and data for hyperscale data center based on distributionally robust CVaR framework
Controlling Compensation Doping via Multivalent Platinum Acceptors in Tantalum Oxide Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterostructures of platinum (Pt) and tantalum oxide (Ta2O5) find widespread use in electronic and energy-conversion device applications, yet the electronic role of Pt incorporated within Ta2O5 remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the influence of Pt incorporation on the electronic structure and properties of amorphous Ta2O5 using two precisely controlled ternary atomic layer deposition (ALD) pathways. Oxygen plasma-enhanced deposition produces host matrices with significantly lower native defect and impurity concentrations than conventional thermal water-based ALD, enabling a systematic investigation of the interplay between Pt dopants and native defects. Controlled Pt incorporation over the range of 0.9–1.9 atom % yields homogeneous, amorphous Pt-doped Ta2O5 thin films containing exclusively Pt(II) and Pt(IV) oxidation states, with no evidence of metallic Pt formation. While the optical bandgap of the Ta2O5 host matrix remains largely unchanged, Pt incorporation introduces optically active acceptor states near the valence band maximum, increases sub-bandgap absorption, and shifts the Fermi level toward the midgap. The relative Pt(II)/Pt(IV) population depends strongly on the defect landscape of the host matrix and exhibits a linear dependence on the Fermi level position, demonstrating Fermi level-controlled charge compensation between native donor defects and multivalent Pt acceptor states. Density functional theory corroborates the acceptor character of Pt and assigns the introduced states primarily to Pt 5d orbitals. Experimentally constructed band diagrams and charge transport measurements further show that Pt incorporation provides a direct means of tuning the electronic properties of Ta2O5. These results demonstrate that multivalent Pt doping serves as a controllable strategy for engineering the electronic structure and transport characteristics of functional Ta2O5 thin films, with direct relevance to memristive, dielectric, and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Host-Defined Trap Polarity Enables Carrier Buffering and Regulates Exciton Dynamics in Deep-Blue MR-TADF OLEDs
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters such as ν-DABNA have enabled highly efficient deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, their device performance is strongly governed by the electronic structure of the host matrix. Here, we demonstrate that ν-DABNA displays a distinct host-dependent reversal of charge-trapping polarity in three representative host matrices—mSiTrz, mCBP, and PhCzBCz in an identical device architecture. Specifically, ν-DABNA behaves as a hole trap in mSiTrz, an electron trap in PhCzBCz, and a bipolar trap in mCBP according to its energy level. The electroluminescence (EL) spectra of ν-DABNA-based devices exhibit nearly identical peak positions around 470 nm, and the mCBP-based device delivers the highest peak EQE at low current density, a relatively serious efficiency roll-off at high current density, and a long device lifetime, indicating the bipolar carrier-buffering effect of doping ν-DABNA. Transient EL measurements reveal a clear decoupling between charge formation and emissive decay processes. The rise dynamics strongly depend on host-dependent trap polarity, leading to a significant variation in turn-on time, while the decay dynamics remain invariant across all devices, confirming that delayed fluorescence is exclusively governed by intrinsic ν-DABNA reverse intersystem crossing (RISC). The temperature-dependent single-carrier current measurement and transient EL decay once again demonstrate the mechanism of carrier trapping and thermal detrapping by ν-DABNA doping in different host systems. Based on these findings, we introduce a host-defined trap-polarity function, ΦH, which quantitatively captures electron–hole transport asymmetry governed by energy-level offsets to link the charge transport and exciton dynamics in ν-DABNA-based MR-TADF OLEDs. This work establishes a universal host-level-controlled trap-assisted emission model for doped MR-TADF OLEDs.

title: Bright-Field-Hidden Disordered Atomic Textures for Physically Unclonable Functions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Optical physical unclonable functions (PUFs) relying on unique microscopic randomness serve as a root of trust for advanced hardware security. However, existing optical PUFs typically rely on disordered structural features at the hundred-nanometer or micrometer scale, facing increasing threats from rapidly advancing 3D nanoprinting technologies. Here, we exploit the atomic-scale thickness irregular texture formed during the epitaxial growth of semiconductor thin films as unclonable nanofingerprints, which demand subnanometer-level precision in the vertical direction for any cloning attempt. Such atomic textures are optically stealthy under bright-field microscopy due to their extremely low thickness. To address this, metallic nanofilms are deposited on the semiconductor surface, enabling the visualization of the patterns via surface plasmonic scattering at the metal nanostep edges under dark-field optical microscopy. The proposed PUF offers advantages, including compatibility with semiconductor fabrication processes, high randomness encoding capacity, bright-field concealment, and strong resilience against physical replication. Based on this PUF, we propose a multilevel key scheme applicable to various application scenarios, demonstrating significant application potential in high-security fields, such as device anticounterfeiting, traceability, information encryption, and authentication.

title: Social acceptance of a green ammonia hub in a remote coastal community – the case of Ísafjörður in Iceland
abstract: The International Maritime Organisation targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by 2050, considering green ammonia to be a promising fuel for decarbonisation. However, development and deployment of this fuel is contingent not only on aspects such as techno-economic feasibility and supportive policy frameworks, but also on social acceptance (SA). This study examines the community-level SA of a potential green ammonia hub for maritime uses in Ísafjörður, Iceland, a remote coastal settlement with a strong maritime history. Based on sixteen semi-structured interviews with local stakeholders, the study identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SA. It reveals that perceived benefits such as job creation and environmental protection function as drivers, while barriers stem from perceived concerns regarding safety, cost, and lack of clear governance. Guided by a community-adapted corporate sustainability classification and a PESTLE lens, identified themes are mapped across political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental dimensions. The findings indicate that political and governance conditions function as an important enabling condition for SA, particularly through the perceived need for clear legislative frameworks and government incentives. Rather than operating independently, these political conditions were closely intertwined with economic and technological considerations, influencing investment risk, infrastructure development, affordability, safety, and equitable benefit distribution. The study concludes that for a just maritime energy transition to succeed, national policymakers must prioritise the implementation of robust incentive mechanisms and strategic roadmaps that satisfactorily address local socio-economic realities and contexts.

title: Türkiye’s gas market reform: A hybrid institutional pathway for competition and resilience
System-level impacts of aeroponics in the bioenergy supply chain: biomass allocation and socio-economic effects
Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
abstract: We use an actor-network concept of translation to examine how EU Renewable Energy Community (REC) policy translates into domestic practice under contested sovereignty, infrastructural isolation, and active geopolitical obstruction. Cyprus is a critical, theory-building case: the EU's last fully isolated grid, occupation of part of its territory by a third state, and Turkish obstruction of both gas exploitation and electricity interconnection make the assumptions embedded in EU policy unusually visible. Drawing on policy documents, twelve interviews and participant observation, we trace how the framework fragments as it moves from supranational design to local implementation. The evidence supports two case-derived hypotheses. The first, presupposition-mismatched translation, holds that compliance fails not for want of will or capacity but because the policy as written presupposes a context that does not exist locally, so translation fragments into competing local interpretations. The second, symmetric foreclosure, holds that where one external mechanism blocks both the domestically prioritised energy-security pathway (gas) and the EU-aligned pathway (interconnected renewable generation), competing local obligatory passage points cancel rather than converge. Their joint product is structural decoupling under material constraint, extending Bromley and Powell's means–ends decoupling to cases where the formal-substantive gap is produced by foreclosure of the prescribed means rather than by organizational choice. The argument is not that RECs cannot exist in Cyprus, but that this decarbonisation initiative receives weak domestic backing for geopolitical rather than technical reasons. We draw implications for green-transition initiatives in other peripheral, geopolitically exposed member states and for differentiated EU implementation guidance.

title: The surprising reason women in academia do more parenting than men
abstract: Policies designed to keep women in the workforce could be entrenching gendered parenting roles.

title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

title: Liquid metal biomimetics: a chemical perspective
abstract: A chemistry-centered framework for Ga-based liquid metal biomimetics, linking multiscale material design and interfacial reactions to matter simulation, energy conversion, information processing and cross-habitat adaptation.

title: Regulating glycerol electrooxidation pathways via catalytic environments
abstract: A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.

title: EGCG@ZIF-8@Polydopamine-Functionalized Janus Nanofibrous Dressing with Directional Exudate Transport and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity for Infected Wound Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The treatment of infected skin wounds continues to face multiple challenges, including bacterial resistance, persistent inflammation, oxidative damage, and inadequate exudate management. To address these issues, a multifunctional Janus wound dressing was constructed to achieve coordinated infection control and tissue repair. Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) was used as a nanocarrier for the natural antioxidant molecule, and polydopamine surface coating endowed the composite nanoparticles with photothermal antibacterial activity. The composite nanoparticles were subsequently incorporated into a hydrophobic polycaprolactone layer by electrospinning and combined with a hydrophilic polyacrylonitrile layer containing a pH indicator, thereby forming a bilayer structure with unidirectional liquid transport, visual monitoring, and wound protection functions. The dressing promotes the outward transfer of wound exudate and produces an observable color response to changes in environmental pH. Under near-infrared irradiation, the antibacterial rate of the dressing reached 98.89% against E. coli and 99.99% against S. aureus. The dressing also possesses excellent free-radical-scavenging capacity, indicating its potential to alleviate excessive oxidative stress in infected wounds. Animal experiments further demonstrated that the dressing reduced the local infection burden, promoted wound closure, collagen deposition, and tissue formation, and caused no obvious histopathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional Janus nanofibrous dressing that integrates antibacterial activity, antioxidant function, exudate regulation, and wound-status monitoring, providing a material-design approach for the repair of infected skin wounds.

title: Synergetic Nano-bending, Photo-switching, and Macrocycle Shuttling Effects of Vibration-Induced Emission Lassos on Photoluminescence Properties of Hydrazone-Based [1]Rotaxanes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 9,14-Diphenyl-9,14-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine (DPAC) fluorophores exhibited large Stokes shifts and vibration-induced emission (VIE) with bistable cyan (at 475 nm) and orange (at 600 nm) emissions, whereas hydrazone fluorophores (cyan emission at 475 nm) underwent reversible Z/E photo-isomerization, enabling efficient photo-switching. Herein, we introduced synergetic nano-bending and photo-switchable effects on optical switchable hydrazone linkers and macrocycle shuttling effects of VIE-active DPAC stoppers in [1]rotaxanes, wherein mechanically interlocked architecture-imposed spatial constraints could modulate photoluminescence (PL) behaviors in response to multiple external stimuli. Surprisingly, the highest lifetime τavg1 = 11.8 ns (cyan emission lifetime monitored at 475 nm) was obtained in the loosened lasso owing to stronger intramolecular hydrogen bonds of hydrazone units with minor constraints of nano-bending. While macrocycle shuttling was acid/base-triggered between the loosened lasso with a near-white-light emission [CIE (0.26, 0.32)] and the tightened lasso with an orange emission [CIE (0.37, 0.36)], [1]rotaxanes could tune synergetic PL emissions by modulating bent/planar conformations of DPAC units via acid/base controls and Z/E photo-isomerization of hydrazone units upon 365/450 nm exposures in isopropanol (IPA), respectively. The non-interlocked analogue exhibited the largest lifetime decrease (Δτavg1 = –1.9 ns), whereas the loosened and tightened lassos showed smaller decreases of Δτavg1 = –1.6 and –0.6 ns, respectively, demonstrating that nano-bending constraints suppressed hydrogen-bond disruption during Z/E photo-isomerization. Furthermore, the loosened lasso exhibited temperature- and viscosity-responsive emissions due to hydrogen-bonding disruptions of hydrazone units and progressive planarization of DPAC units upon heating to induce lower viscosity. These results highlight the potential of [1]rotaxanes as stimuli-responsive luminescent molecular systems, enabling proof-of-concept demonstrations in temperature and viscosity sensing as well as optical information encoding.

title: Towards smart city energy-transportation coupling system resilience enhancement via multi-type mobile emergency resources: a hybrid data-model driven approach
Heterophase-Engineered Cs3Cu2I5/CsCu2I3 Memristors with Two-Step Resistive Switching
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The quest for energy-efficient memory technologies is critically hindered by the performance gap between high-performing but toxic lead-based perovskites and their environmentally benign yet less reliable lead-free counterparts. Here, we address this challenge by engineering the controlled coexistence of crystallographically 0D Cs3Cu2I5 and 1D CsCu2I3 phases using a scalable, hot-air-assisted process. The resulting heterophase architecture produces composition-dependent structural, interfacial, and chemical environments that strongly influence resistive-switching behavior. The optimized devices exhibit a high ON/OFF ratio of up to 7.4 × 108, more than three orders of magnitude higher than that of the corresponding single-phase films, together with electroforming-free operation and a reproducible two-step SET process that provides distinct resistance states for multilevel memory operation. Combined electrical, XPS, cross-sectional STEM/EDS, and post-switching ToF-SIMS analyses support a hybrid valence-change memory/electrochemical metallization (VCM-ECM) filament-evolution framework involving halide-deficient pathways, Cu–O-related oxygen-containing environments, and redistribution of Ag- and Cu-containing species. The two-step SET behavior and two threshold-like regions in the log–log I–V characteristics are consistent with multistage changes in trap occupancy and conductive-path connectivity without requiring direct assignment of the individual transitions to specific vacancy species. These results demonstrate heterophase engineering as an effective materials strategy for regulating local ionic and electronic transport in lead-free halide memristors and provide a pathway toward high-performance, multilevel nonvolatile memory and other ionically active solid-state devices.

title: Interfacial Origin of Mn Promotion in Ni/AlO x Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis and Carbon Nanotube Growth
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Commercial deployment of methane pyrolysis (MP) requires H2 to be produced at a high rate while the solid carbon is recovered as a marketable product such as multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). Various promoters have been explored for Ni-based MP catalysts, including Mn, but the origin of its effect has remained elusive. Here, Ni/AlOx catalysts containing 0 to 5 wt % Mn were used to separate the two roles that Mn plays in activity and stability. The amount of Ni exposed at an oxide boundary correlated with the apparent CH4 reaction order across the series, identifying the Ni–O–Mn perimeter as the site at which CH4 activation is promoted. The same perimeter converted weakly bound NiO into strongly interacting species that resisted encapsulation, linking the rate and the lifetime of the catalyst to a single interface. At 1 wt %, Mn the apparent activation energy fell from 93.9 to 84.2 kJ mol–1, the CH4 reaction order rose from 0.46 to 0.84, and the turnover number increased from 375 to 456 mol C mol Ni–1. At 2 wt %, MnOx began to bury the Ni surface, and above that loading it segregated into a separate phase, so the promotion was lost. Mn also improved the graphitization and conductivity of the MWCNTs formed at the start of the reaction, but this benefit faded as disordered carbon accumulated. Co-feeding H2 suppressed this accumulation and gave MWCNTs with an electrical conductivity comparable to that of commercial material. The benefit of Mn is therefore set by where it resides rather than by how much is added, and both products of MP reach useful quality only when the promoter loading and the reaction conditions are optimized together.

title: Probing Counterion Distribution Around Cationic Metal–Organic Cages by Fluorescence, Analytical Ultracentrifugation, and Molecular Dynamics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report a convenient fluorescence-based approach to probe the counterion association around soluble, cationic metal–organic cages (MOCs) in aqueous solution. Two MOCs incorporating tetra-(4-pyridylphenyl) ethylene (TPPE), an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) chromophore, were employed to monitor the spatial distribution and binding of counter-anions across a range of ionic strengths. Alterations in the fluorescence response of the TPPE groups sensitively respond to the changes in their local environment, providing a probe of counterion location and distribution. The results suggest a stepwise counter-anion association mechanism around MOCs: first around the Pt vertices dominated by electrostatic interactions at low counterion-to-MOC ratios, then interacting with the TPPE ligands at higher ratios. Analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) results and all-atom molecular dynamics simulations are in good agreement with this proposed two-stage association mechanism and suggest distinct spatial preferences of different anions. This combined experimental–computational strategy provides a broadly applicable method for elucidating counterion distributions and dynamics around charged nanoscale species in solution.

title: Nanozymes as Heterogeneous Catalysts: In Operando Aggregation and Altered Apparent Substrate Affinity Affect Catalytic Properties and Immunoassay Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanozymes are synthetic nanoscale catalysts that are actively explored as functional replacements for natural enzymes in various applications. Often, the properties and characteristics of enzymes are directly transferred to nanozymes without considering their unique features as nanosized heterogeneous catalysts. In this article, we explore two often-neglected factors: reduced substrate binding and aggregation of peroxidase-mimicking nanozyme particles that occur in operando (i.e., during catalysis or sample incubation). A competitive Langmuir–Hinshelwood model was utilized to evaluate the impact of organic solvent on substrate binding. In operando aggregation of Au@Pt particles was confirmed by visible spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and ultramicroscopy. We demonstrate that both reduced substrate binding and aggregation significantly affect the kinetic parameters of nanozyme catalysis, including approximately three-fold decrease of the apparent Michaelis–Menten constant, a six-fold decrease of the maximum reaction rate, and erroneous conclusions regarding activity inhibition. The effect of aggregation was studied in microplate immunoassays and lateral flow immunoassays of Staphylococcal enterotoxin A (SEA). The results demonstrate that aggregation leads to a reduced specific signal (from immunocomplexes of SEA with Au@Pt-mAb) and an increased nonspecific signal (from aggregated Au@Pt), resulting in a lower signal-to-noise ratio. As a consequence, this leads to false-positive results in microplate immunoassays or even ruins lateral flow immunoassay performance. These results confirm that in operando colloidal stability and substrate binding are crucial factors to be considered for the accurate quantification of kinetic parameters and for various bioanalytical applications.

title: Quantifying Effective van der Waals Interactions Across Two-Dimensional Material Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a central role in determining the properties and functionality of two-dimensional (2D) materials and their heterostructures. However, quantitative nanoscale characterization of these interactions remains challenging. Here, we introduce a universal multifrequency atomic force microscopy (AFM) framework for quantitative mapping of effective vdW interaction landscapes and the extraction of effective Hamaker constants with Ångström-scale vertical resolution. Using graphene, graphene oxide, hexagonal boron nitride, molybdenum disulfide, and highly oriented pyrolytic graphite as model systems, we systematically investigate the influence of layer number, substrate, defects, step edges, surface roughness, and functionalization on local vdW interactions. The measurements reveal pronounced spatial variations and nonadditive behavior, demonstrating that effective Hamaker constants can be enhanced or suppressed by nanoscale structural and interfacial features. This work provides a rapid and versatile approach for nanoscale characterization of vdW interactions and offers new opportunities for engineering interfacial forces in 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures.

title: High-Entropy Design of Commensurate Antiferroelectric Ceramics with Superior Energy Storage Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramic dielectrics are imperative for next-generation energy-storage capacitors because of near-zero remnant polarization. In this work, we construct a new high-entropy antiferroelectric ceramic to synergistically optimize dielectric energy storage by reconstructing the commensurate polarization modulation, thereby delivering an ultrahigh recoverable energy density (Wrec) of ∼14.2 J/cm3 at 71 kV/mm while maintaining a high energy efficiency (η) of ∼84%. In addition, the ceramics deliver remarkable fatigue resistance with stable performance over 105 charge–discharge cycles. This study highlights entropy engineering as a powerful framework for designing high-performance AFE energy-storage ceramics and offers insights for the future development of advanced dielectric capacitors.

title: Synergistic Catalysis at the Ni3Te2–Ni3C Heterointerface: Accelerating Water Dissociation for Efficient and Robust Hydrogen Evolution in Alkaline Water and Seawater
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is kinetically limited by sluggish interfacial water dissociation and the subsequent hydrogen intermediate conversion, making the cooperative regulation of consecutive HER elementary steps crucial for achieving efficient electrocatalysis. However, most reported HER heterostructures primarily rely on global electronic structure modulation, while function-oriented interfacial regulation of distinct reaction steps remains insufficiently explored. Herein, a Ni3Te2–Ni3C heterostructure electrode was in situ fabricated on nickel foam via a one-step electrodeposition strategy and systematically evaluated for HER in both alkaline freshwater and alkaline seawater. Mechanistic investigations indicate that Ni3C promotes interfacial water activation and dissociation, whereas the Ni3Te2–Ni3C heterointerface further optimizes the kinetics of hydrogen intermediate conversion, thereby enabling the cooperative regulation of consecutive HER elementary steps. In situ Raman spectroscopy, together with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, provides supportive evidence for the facilitated water dissociation and optimized hydrogen intermediate conversion at the heterointerface. Benefiting from such functional complementarity, the optimized Ni3Te2–Ni3C/NF electrode requires overpotentials of only 26 and 32 mV to achieve 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH and alkaline seawater, respectively, while maintaining good stability under the investigated operating conditions. This work establishes a structure–interface–activity relationship and provides a reaction pathway-oriented design principle for developing efficient alkaline HER electrocatalysts.

title: Decoupling Electrochemical Performance from External Pressure via Mechanically Interlocked 3D Interfaces for Ultra-low-pressure Supercapacitor Pouch Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Supercapacitor pouch cells typically require substantial external stack pressure (typically >2 MPa) to maintain intimate internal interface contact. However, the heavy packaging modules introduce significant inactive mass, reducing system-level energy density. Herein, we report a two-step aligned 3D imprinting strategy that fundamentally decouples electrochemical performance from external compression. By engineering a mechanically interlocked structure, the compaction force is precisely directed toward the interfaces between the active particles, as well as between the particles and the current collector. This prevents lateral slippage, achieving ultra-low internal electrode resistance and conformal interface contact. Consequently, compared with planar electrodes, imprinted electrodes exhibit a 14.3-fold lower interfacial resistance and a 2.7-fold lower equivalent series resistance even under 0.3 MPa stack pressure, delivering an unprecedented average power density of 285 kW kg–1 at 1 mg cm–2 and 28.4 kW kg–1 at 5 mg cm–2. Notably, pouch cells based on 3D-D electrodes sustain 100,000 cycles with 99% capacitance retention, benefiting from the mechanically stabilized interface and the suppressed resistance evolution. Furthermore, this paradigm is compatible with roll-to-roll manufacturing processes, providing a versatile and scalable approach for the next generation of high-power, lightweight, and ultra-low-pressure supercapacitor systems.

title: A Sequentially Disassembling Nanocomposite Hydrogel with Lesion-Triggered Luteolin Release for Multitarget Acne Vulgaris Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Acne vulgaris (AV) remains challenging to treat due to antibiotic resistance, side effects, and the lack of topical formulations that concomitantly eradicate Cutibacterium acnes, resolve inflammation, and restore redox homeostasis. Here, we report a sequentially pH-disassembling nanocomposite hydrogel (TCL2.16‰@PQ; PQ represents poly(vinyl alcohol)/quaternized chitosan (PVA/QCS)) for comprehensive AV management, in which tannic acid/Cu2+/luteolin metal–phenolic network nanoparticles (TCL NPs) serve as both drug reservoirs and physical crosslinking nodes within PVA/QCS (PQ) matrix. The hydrogel optimally disassembles at pH 6.5, followed by TCL NP disassembly at pH 6.0, enabling microenvironment-triggered release of luteolin preferentially at the AV lesion site (5.0–7.5, 6.35 ± 1.30; healthy individuals: 4.1–5.8). This design enhances skin permeation flux by 1.5-fold compared to TCL NPs alone. Additionally, the hydrogel's shear-thinning and thixotropic properties make it easy to spread and adhere to the skin. In vitro, the hydrogel completely eradicates Cutibacterium acnes and reduces biofilm biomass by 7.6-fold at 0.2 g/mL, polarizes macrophages to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, and scavenges reactive oxygen species through direct radical scavenging and upregulation of SOD/GPx/HO-1. In a murine AV model, the hydrogel achieved complete bacterial eradication and lesion resolution within 14 days, significantly outperforming a commercial metronidazole gel by concurrently reducing inflammation and restoring redox homeostasis. This work establishes a microenvironment-responsive, multitarget nanocomposite platform addressing the core pathogenic factors of AV, presenting a promising alternative to conventional therapies.

title: Memory-Enhanced Visible-Light Photonic Synapses in Interface-Engineered ZnON/IGZO Oxide Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Zinc oxynitride (ZnON) thin-film transistors (TFTs) are attractive visible-light photoactive devices owing to their narrow and tunable optical bandgap; however, the limited population of deep-level trap states can restrict post-illumination carrier retention, resulting in weak photonic synaptic retention. Here, memory-enhanced visible-light photonic synapses are demonstrated using interface-engineered ZnON/Indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) double-layer oxide TFTs. A thin IGZO capping layer is integrated onto the ZnON channel to preserve ZnON-dominated red, green, and blue (RGB) photoresponse, while modifying the interfacial electronic environment and carrier-relaxation dynamics. The ZnON/IGZO TFT exhibits RGB responsivities of 2.93, 11.0, and 17.6 A W–1 and specific detectivities of 1.10 × 1012, 3.82 × 1012, and 6.08 × 1012 Jones under red, green, and blue illumination, respectively. The device also exhibits enhanced short- and long-term synaptic retention behavior under pulsed optical stimulation, wavelength-dependent synaptic plasticity, and analogue synaptic weight modulation. Spectroscopic ellipsometry and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal that the IGZO capping layer preserves ZnON-dominated visible-light absorption, while inducing changes in oxygen-related bonding environments across the bilayer structure. Photoinduced current transient spectroscopy reveals a redistribution of electrically active trap states toward both relatively shallow- and deep-level regions after IGZO capping. The shallow-level states are correlated with enhanced photoresponse, whereas the deep-level states are consistent with delayed carrier relaxation and prolonged post-illumination retention. These results demonstrate that ZnON/IGZO bilayer engineering provides an effective strategy for coupling broadband visible-light sensitivity with tunable carrier-retention dynamics in oxide photonic synapses.

title: A multi-metric framework for tidal stream resource and load characterization: Application to Cook Inlet, Alaska
Spatially Programmed Water Access Reconciles Service Stability with Triggered Post-Use Degradation in Biobased Multilayer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable packaging plastics often face a fundamental paradox: the material must resist moisture and remain stable during service, yet undergo controlled disassembly after disposal. Therefore, sustainable materials should not be evaluated solely based on their service performance or degradation rate, but rather on their ability to undergo effective functional transitions at critical stages throughout the lifecycle. Here, we developed a spatially programmed design strategy that addresses these conflicting requirements by regulating not only when and where water enters the material, but also how the degradation proceeds. The film consists of a hydrophilic, pectin-based inner layer, a hydrophobic polylactic acid (PLA) outer layer, and a hydrogen-bonded interface formed via hydrogen bonding. During packaging service, the PLA layer acts as a moisture-shielding skin, maintaining wet stability, barrier performance, and mechanical integrity. A key conceptual advance of this work lies in turning an inherent weakness into a lifecycle-regulating function, where water sensitivity serves as a trigger rather than a limitation. After use, assisted by mechanical damage, water activates the pectin/deep eutectic solvent (DES) phase. The acidic, water-rich microenvironment generated by the pectin/DES supports preferential cleavage near the PLA chain ends, promoting progressive molecular weight reduction while preventing premature failure that could compromise service performance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further establish a molecular-level structure–function relationship within the architecture. The calculated interfacial binding energies and molecular interactions elucidate the origin of structural stability during service, while comparative analysis of PLA ester bond cleavage pathways demonstrates a more favorable energetic pathway for terminal ester cleavage after activation, supporting the chain-end-preferential degradation tendency. In contrast to conventional multilayer materials that mainly improve individual properties, this work provides insights into biopolymer design, moving beyond the long-standing trade-off paradigm of stability and degradability by spatially programming these functions as complementary components within a lifecycle-balanced architecture.

title: Pain-Perception-Inspired Neuromorphic Sensing: Nonmonotonic Electrical Response and Spatial Visualization in a Near-Infrared-Responsive MXene Hydrogel
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic sensory devices that encode environmental stimuli at the sensing interface offer a route toward more adaptive machine–environment interactions. Ionic hydrogels provide mechanically compliant, ion-conducting hydrated networks that can incorporate photothermal components. However, many near-infrared (NIR)-responsive hydrogels show conductivity changes in one direction, while terminal electrical signals provide little information about stimulus location. Achieving response-direction reversal and spatially resolved visual feedback in one soft material using a single NIR input, therefore, remains challenging. Inspired by protective inhibition and post-stimulus rebound in pain-related neural signaling, we developed an NIR neuromorphic sensory device based on a Ca–PAA–EMB@IL-MXene hydrogel. The material couples photothermal conversion by IL-MXene with temperature-dependent ion transport in a hydrated Ca2+-coordinated PAA-EMB network. Weak irradiation transiently enhances conductivity, whereas stronger or prolonged irradiation drives the conductivity through a maximum into a suppressed state, followed by rebound and recovery after stimulus removal. Thermal, electrical, optical, and water-state measurements are consistent with heat-induced water redistribution and reorganization of the hydrated network, with the characteristic transition temperatures regulated by the EMB content. Programmed NIR pulses further produce paired-pulse facilitation-like behavior, signal accumulation, and responses dependent on recent stimulation history. Localized irradiation induces reversible whitening in the exposed region, supplementing the overall electrical signal with spatial information. An impedance-acquisition and microcontroller interface converts these responses into initial, strong-stimulus warning, and recovery states. This work provides a soft-material strategy for encoding NIR stimulus intensity, duration, history, and location through coupled electrical and optical outputs, supporting NIR-responsive neuromorphic sensing and warning interfaces.

title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO2, and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO2-starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO2 reduction under dilute CO2. By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–Nx sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO2 adduct that enhances local CO2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO2 reduction catalysts under CO2-limited conditions.

title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. However, a general reductionist framework for rationally constructing CVs remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of the minimal motifs required to drive coacervates into stable vesicular topologies. Here, we present a protein language model-informed design of such minimal systems, where arginine-rich oligopeptides and competing anionic oligomers self-assemble into oligo-coacervate vesicles (OCVs) without any chemical modifications or external fuels. Combining experiments and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate an assembly mechanism governed by an electrostatic-hydrophobic balance, which enables vesiculation across a broad range of oligomer pairs. This principle further permits de novo functionalization, exemplified by OCVs engineered to selectively recognize and encapsulate DNA G-quadruplex structures. Together, these findings establish sequence-encoded design rules for the predictable construction of vesicle-like compartments.

title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species (Arabidopsis, maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k-mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants.
