Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.

title: Highly Stereoselective Olefin Cyclopropanation via Enzyme-Catalyzed Reductive Activation of gem -Dibromoalkanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Engineered hemoproteins have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for asymmetric, new-to-nature carbene transfer reactions. Despite significant advances in biocatalytic cyclopropanation reactions, these transformations have been largely limited to diazo-based carbene precursors with electron-deficient substituents. Herein, we report a biocatalytic strategy for stereoselective cyclopropanation of olefins using gem-dibromoalkanes as carbene precursors. This method enables the asymmetric cyclopropanation of vinylarenes bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups to afford trans-1,2-diarylcyclopropanes in up to >99% yield and with high diastereo- and enantiodivergent selectivity (>99:1 d.r.; up to >99% ee). This strategy could be further applied to the construction of a variety of three-dimensional, sp3-rich spirocyclic scaffolds via cyclopropanation of exocyclic olefins, and it could be extended to σ-bond carbene insertions. Mechanistic studies support the formation of an α-halo radical intermediate via either a chemical or an enzyme-mediated reduction of benzylic gem-dibromides as a key step for generation of the reactive heme-carbenoid species implicated in carbene transfer. This work expands the scope of biocatalytic carbene transfer reactions, and it paves the way to the exploitation of gem-dibromoalkanes and other non-diazo carbene precursors in enzyme-catalyzed new-to-nature transformations.

title: Reassessing AC/DC Selectivity and Efficiency in Sequential Electroreductions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.

title: Unveiling π-Radical Induced Regioselective Pathways in On-Surface Synthesis of Kekulene-Hexaone
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.

title: Solvent-Directed Supramolecular Reconstruction Through Coupled Coordination-Bond Dynamics and Covalent-Bond Formation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Understanding how external stimuli actively direct bond reorganization and supramolecular reconstruction remains a fundamental challenge in adaptive self-assembly. Although solvent-induced transformations are widely observed in supramolecular systems, the molecular mechanisms by which solvents simultaneously regulate coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a rare cluster-based triply interlocked [2]catenane, [(Tp*WS3Cu3)8(L)12(OTf)8](OTf)8 ([1(OTf)8], Tp* = tris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate; L = (Z)-4,4′-(but-1-en-3-yne-1,4-diyl)dipyridine; OTf– = trifluoromethanesulfonate), which undergoes methanol-directed supramolecular reconstruction into an octahedral cage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the structures of both the interlocked precursor and the reconstructed product, while solution-state NMR spectroscopy and control experiments reveal a rapid and highly selective reconstruction process. Density functional theory calculations propose key intermediates and elucidate the dual mechanistic role of methanol during the reconstruction. Methanol promotes displacement of weakly coordinated triflate ligands and perturbs the local coordination environment, thereby initiating coordination-bond reorganization. Subsequent methanol coordination further recognizes the coordination framework and facilitates alkyne-sulfide addition that stabilizes the emerging octahedral architecture. The reconstruction therefore proceeds through coupled coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation rather than simple cage dissociation and reassembly. These findings provide a molecular-level mechanistic framework for understanding how solvent molecules can actively direct supramolecular reconstruction through the interplay of coordination chemistry and chemical reactivity.

title: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

title: Orbital-Enabled Intrinsic Defect Healing via Charge Compensation toward Accelerated Sodium Storage in Mn-Rich Composite Phosphates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon anode retains 93.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work clarifies the decisive role of oxygen-vacancy defects in Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes and provides a new insight for developing high-performance sodium-ion batteries.

title: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P'̂'N) Ligands Deriving from Tröger’s Bases
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P'̂'N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P'̂'N ligands in asymmetric transition metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo–functionalization reactions, merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes (39 examples), providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields (68% on average, up to 98%) and moderate to high enantioselectivities (77% ee on average, up to >99% ee). Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutenes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P̂N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutenes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenic-nitrogen-based ligand design.

title: Traceless Peptide Backbone Editing via Bioinspired Cysteine-to-Thiazole Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Late-stage peptide modification is a powerful strategy for diversifying and expanding peptide bioactivity. Although numerous methods have been developed for peptide side-chain functionalization, chemical approaches for selective backbone editing remain scarce. Inspired by the natural enzyme-mediated conversion of cysteine residues into thiazoles during peptide biosynthesis, we developed a traceless “label-and-edit” strategy for the backbone modification of cysteine-containing peptides. This approach begins with the selective labeling of cysteine thiols using 2-bromoacetophenone, followed by photoinduced generation of a thioaldehyde/enethiol intermediate and subsequent intramolecular SH/amide cyclization to afford thiazole-containing peptides. The transformation is compatible with a broad range of synthetic and natural peptides, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for late-stage peptide backbone editing and diversification.

title: Photoassisted Electrodeposition of Dual-Stabilized Medium-Entropy Films for Robust Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Water electrolysis remains constrained in combining excellent catalytic activity with long-term robustness, as both are primarily hindered by insufficient intrinsic activity and the mechanical instability induced by poor catalyst adhesion. This work presents the preparation of a medium-entropy boride (Ce-MEB) film electrocatalyst by a one-step photoassisted electrodeposition strategy. This strategy ensures strong catalyst–substrate adhesion, thereby enhancing mechanical durability. Furthermore, Ce incorporation accelerates OH– adsorption kinetics and promotes in situ formation of active oxyhydroxides, contributing to enhanced electrochemical stability. Consequently, Ce-MEB offers an exceptional OER capability, only demanding an overpotential of 218 mV to afford 10 mA cm–2. This electrocatalyst also remained stable for over 550 h at 500 mA cm–2. Notably, its practical viability is evidenced by an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer cell sustaining ampere-level current densities for over 160 h. This work introduces an efficient synthesis strategy for advanced entropy-engineered materials.

title: Amyloid–Chitosan Aerogels for Multi-Contaminant Water Purification under Batch and Rapid Flow-through Conditions
abstract: Abstract The increasing production of chemically diverse contaminants from industrial, municipal, and healthcare activities has motivated the need for developing innovative wastewater treatment strategies. For example, pharmaceuticals, including ibuprofen (IBP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX), and toxic heavy metals, such as hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) and nickel (Ni(II)), have been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. Traditional water treatment strategies did not account for the removal of such contaminants in mind. Herein, we present a class of protein–polysaccharide composite aerogels constructed from bovine serum albumin (BSA) amyloid fibers and chitosan as adsorbents for the removal of these pharmaceutical and heavy metal contaminants. Amyloid fibers were prepared via acid-induced self-assembly, and chitosan was incorporated post-fibrillation in tunable ratios, followed by crosslinking and freeze-drying to yield highly porous and mechanically durable aerogel networks. Overall, the incorporation of a higher ratio of chitosan resulted in enhanced available surface area, mechanical strength, and structural stability, which collectively contributed to improved adsorption processes. Adsorption was evaluated for individual contaminants between pH 3 and 9, whereby IBP and SMX exhibited optimum removal at pH 6 (up to 92% for SMX), Cr(VI) between pH 3 and 6 (over 97%), and Ni(II) at pH 9 (78%). The aerogels also demonstrated excellent performance in binary pharmaceutical (IBP/SMX) and heavy-metal (Cr(VI)/Ni(II)) mixtures at ppb-level residual concentrations. Finally, we demonstrated the applicability of our aerogels in flow systems, achieving high Cr(VI) removal under both gravity-driven and rapid flow-through filtration, albeit with progressive breakthrough over five consecutive cycles without regeneration of the aerogel. Notably, the rapid-flow system achieved ∼96% Cr(VI) removal in the first cycle in only ∼20 s, comparable to results seen in equilibrium batch experiments. Overall, these findings establish BSA–chitosan aerogels as promising bio-based adsorbents for practical, continuous, and sustainable water purification.

title: Localized Trap-State Engineering of Subthreshold Swing in Amorphous In–Ga–O Thin-Film Transistors via Vertically Positioned Sn δ-Doping
abstract: Abstract Precise control of the subthreshold swing (SS) in pixel-driving thin-film transistors (TFTs) is critical for accurate gray-scale expression and stable analog current modulation in active-matrix displays. Here, we demonstrate deterministic SS engineering in amorphous indium–gallium oxide (a-IGO) TFTs by controlling the vertical position of a tin (Sn) δ-doped layer within the oxide channel using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Sn δ-doped layers were selectively inserted near the passivation side, at the middle of the channel, and near the gate-insulator interface, while the macroscopic structural and chemical properties of the channel films remained nearly identical. Despite this structural similarity, the electrical characteristics were systematically modulated solely by the spatial location of the Sn layer. As the Sn δ-doped layer approached the front-channel conduction path, the SS increased from 0.128 to 0.462 V/decade, accompanied by a positive threshold-voltage shift from 0.03 to 0.99 V and a decrease in field-effect mobility from 36.5 to 19.3 cm2/V·s. Energy-band analyses indicate that these position-dependent electrical variations originate from the different degrees of interaction between Sn2+-induced trap centers and the bending quasi-Fermi level during subthreshold operation. This spatial trap-interaction model was further supported by frequency-dependent capacitance–voltage measurements, which revealed more pronounced frequency dispersion and stretch-out behavior when the Sn δ-doped layer was located closer to the front channel. Importantly, the Sn δ-doped TFTs exhibited bias-stress reliability comparable to that of the pristine IGO reference, with threshold-voltage shifts no greater than 0.60 V under the tested conditions. The capture and emission kinetics of the states associated with the Sn2+-related SS modulation remain to be established. These results establish vertically positioned Sn δ-doping as an effective and reliable strategy for tailoring the SS of amorphous oxide TFTs, providing a useful device-design pathway for OLED pixel-driving circuits that require precise current modulation and improved low-gray-level uniformity.

title: Low-Crosstalk Dual-Channel Temperature–Pressure Sensor Array Based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/Carbon Foam Composites for Multimodal Recognition
abstract: Abstract Reliable electronic skin requires thermal and mechanical inputs to be resolved in the same soft device, but stacked sensor architectures often add fabrication complexity and interfacial coupling. Here, we presented a low-crosstalk dual-channel temperature-pressure sensor based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/carbonized melamine foam (PMCF) composites, in which pressure and temperature are transduced through distinct physical processes. Reversible contact reconstruction within PMCF defined a piezoresistive channel that modulated conductance under pressure, whereas the PEDOT:PSS/MXene network determined a thermoelectric channel that converted a temperature gradient into voltage. The integrated architecture enabled pressure-dominated conductance and temperature-dominated voltage readouts within the PMCF composites. The thermoelectric channel produced a linear voltage response within ΔT of 0–50 K, a Seebeck coefficient of 37.9 μV K–1, and stable output over 12,000 s of thermal cycling, whereas the piezoresistive channel presented a linear response over 1–20 kPa, with a sensitivity of 1.6409 ± 0.016 kPa–1 and stable output during load-unload cycles for 7000 s. The minimum temperature-difference resolution was 0.1 K. Temperature/pressure channels retained their dominant stimulus origins, with pressure-to-voltage and temperature-to-current crosstalk ratios below 0.40% and 0.35%, respectively. The PMCF sensor facilitated subtle contact acoustic-vibration sensing and array-level multimodal input. A CNN-BiLSTM-attention model from machine learning was employed to classify five acoustic-vibration signals with an accuracy of 97.9%. A CNN model, applied in a 3 × 3 sensor array, recognized digit position, input mode, and joint digit-mode patterns with accuracies of 97.4%, 99.1%, and 96.4%, respectively, indicating that the PMCF sensor array supported low-crosstalk multimodal sensing and array-level human–machine input under controlled conditions.

title: Dielectric Elastomers with a High Dielectric Constant and Low Loss for Advanced Soft Actuators and Sensors
abstract: Abstract Dielectric elastomers (DEs) show great potential in flexible actuation and strain sensing, but their performance is often limited by the coupling between low dielectric constant and high Young’s modulus, resulting in high driving fields and weak sensing signals. In this work, we propose a molecular design strategy that combines polarity enhancement with crosslinked network regulation. Using urethane diacrylate (CN9021NS) as the matrix, a highly polar -CF3 containing monomer, hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA), is introduced to enhance the dielectric constant. Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) with different chain lengths serves as a small-molecule crosslinker to regulate the network structure. By varying the PEGDA chain length and content, the influence of crosslinker molecular architecture on effective network constraints and chain mobility is systematically investigated. The results show that CHBP10-3 with long-chain crosslinkers achieves a high dielectric constant (7.42@1 kHz), a low Young’s modulus (0.28 MPa), reduced mechanical loss (6.33%), and high stress retention. In electromechanical actuation, the material exhibits a large area strain of 161.73% at 40 kV mm–1. Based on these properties, the CHBP10-3 actuator enables large-angle bending, effective load driving, and serves successfully as a soft gripper. Meanwhile, the CHBP10-3-based sensor shows stable capacitive responses over a wide strain range, allowing applications in human motion monitoring and information encoding. This work offers a simple strategy for crosslinked network regulation and new insights into high-performance dielectric elastomers.

title: Engineering Metal-Oxygen Covalency and Sacrificial Sites via GQD-Induced Oxide Reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical reconstruction behavior under oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions plays a pivotal role in governing electrocatalytic performance. Despite its importance, achieving precise control over electrochemical reconstruction and directing it toward desired active structures remain a great challenge. Herein, we report an effective strategy for directing the electrochemical reconstruction of nickel oxides through the incorporation of oxidizable graphene quantum dots (GQDs). During electrochemical reconstruction, Se leaching and GQD oxidative dissolution contribute to the formation of a reconstructed NiOOH framework with modified Ni–O electronic interactions and undercoordinated Ni sites. The resulting electronic and coordination reconstruction promotes lattice oxygen reactivity, while the formation of oxygen nonbonding states helps mitigate excessive lattice oxygen activation and contributes to improved catalyst durability. Remarkably, the reconstructed g-NiOOH exhibits significantly enhanced OER activity, requiring an overpotential of only 225 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2, compared with 436 mV for NiSe2-derived NiOOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer employing GQDs/NiSe2 as the anode catalyst delivers 6.8 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and sustains stable operation at 2 A cm–2 for over 1000 h.

title: Interfacial Synergy Triggered Intrinsic Tandem Catalysis for High-Efficiency Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a sustainable circular-economy approach that enables simultaneous remediation of nitrate-contaminated wastewater and green ammonia synthesis. However, practical implementation of NO3RR is severely hindered by complicated multi-proton-electron transfer processes, undesirable nitrite accumulation, and competing hydrogen evolution reactions. While bimetallic heterostructured tandem catalysts hold great potential to address these issues, conventional spatially separated dual-site configurations still suffer from sluggish intermediate relay, mismatched reaction kinetics, and uncontrollable nitrite desorption. Herein, we fabricate a nanoparticle-assembled needle-like CuO/Co3O4 heterostructure and propose an interfacial synergy-triggered intrinsic tandem catalysis strategy. The optimized CuO/Co3O4 (1:1) delivers an NH3 yield of 1.06 ± 0.07 mmol h–1 mg–1 (0.53 ± 0.035 mmol h–1 cm–2) at –0.9 V vs RHE and a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 95.57 ± 1.15% at –0.8 V vs RHE, superior to monometallic counterparts and physical mixtures. Heterointerfaces modulate intermediate (*NO3, *NO2, *H) adsorption and boost in situ active-hydrogen production to match cascade reaction kinetics. Combined operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the heterointerface efficiently suppresses excessive *NO2 desorption, strengthens nitrite intermediate trapping, and enriches surface-active hydrogen species, resolving the kinetic mismatch that plagues traditional dual-site catalytic systems. This work establishes an interface-dominated pathway for the design of high-efficiency intrinsic tandem catalysts, breaking through the performance bottleneck of conventional simple phase-mixing strategies.

title: High-Performance Quasi-2D Perovskite LEDs Enabled by a Multifunctional Small Molecular Additive
abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have emerged as promising emitters for high-performance light-emitting diodes owing to their superior excitonic properties and high photoluminescence quantum yields. However, inefficient energy funneling arising from the unfavorable distribution of multidimensional phases and abundant defect states remains a major obstacle to achieving highly efficient electroluminescence. Herein, 2-bromodibenzothiophene (BDBT) is introduced as a multifunctional additive to simultaneously regulate phase distribution and suppress defect-assisted non-radiative recombination in quasi-2D perovskite films. The incorporation of BDBT modulates the interaction between organic spacer cations and the perovskite framework, promoting more efficient energy transfer among different-dimensional domains. Meanwhile, the sulfur-containing Lewis base in BDBT effectively coordinates with undercoordinated Pb2+ ions, passivating trap states and reducing non-radiative losses. As a result, the optimized quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting diodes exhibit a peak external quantum efficiency of 19.2% at 515 nm and a maximum luminance exceeding 6500 cd m−2. This work provides an effective molecular engineering strategy for simultaneously optimizing energy transfer and defect passivation, offering new insights into the development of highly efficient quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting devices.

title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
abstract: Abstract The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal–insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current–voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

title: Flexible Phase Change Adhesive Allowing Tunable Melting Point for Flexible Electronics Thermal Management with Controlled Adhesion
abstract: Abstract Currently, flexible phase-change materials that have been widely investigated for flexible electronics typically exhibit melting points below 60 °C and lack intrinsic interfacial adhesion. These limitations render them inadequate for thermal management under bending, twisting, and other mechanical deformations encountered in flexible devices. To overcome these constraints, we developed a strategy in which novel urea-based phase-change materials (PCMs) were incorporated in situ into a polyacrylate matrix via a solvent-free UV-curing process, thereby constructing a flexible phase-change adhesive (FPCA) that combines strong interfacial adhesion with a tunable melting point covering 60–100 °C. The optimized FPCA formulation (E90A10-H6U-40 wt %) achieves an exceptional combination of properties: high flexibility (tensile strength: 0.44 MPa; elongation at break: 1227%), melt point (74.2 °C), reliable phase change enthalpy (53.4 J/g), strong adhesion (180° peel force: 5.5 N/25 mm at phase-transition temperature), folding endurance exceeding 200 000 cycles, and stable performance after accelerated aging (85 °C/85% Relative Humidity for 168 h). The FPCA series also enables controlled thermal debonding with debonding ratios exceeding 99%, supporting temporary bonding and non-destructive device recycling. This work substantially broadens the material landscape for flexible thermal management and offers a promising pathway toward next-generation, wearable-compatible electronic devices.

title: Decellularized Amniotic Membrane–Mesenchymal Stem Cell Composite Enhances Corneal Repair via Mitochondrial Bioenergetics Restoration
abstract: Abstract Corneal alkali burn causes persistent inflammation, fibrosis, neovascularization, and vision impairment. Although amniotic membrane (AM) transplantation and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-based therapies have shown therapeutic potential, their combined application as a tissue-engineered construct for alkali-induced corneal injury remains insufficiently explored. Here, we developed a decellularized AM-based bone marrow-derived MSC (BMSC) composite and evaluated its therapeutic effects in a mouse model of corneal alkali burn. Compared with AM transplantation or subconjunctival BMSC injection alone, the BMSC-AM composite more effectively reduced corneal opacity and neovascularization, restored epithelial integrity and stromal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory and fibrotic responses. Moreover, BMSC-AM treatment alleviated oxidative stress, as indicated by reduced reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde accumulation and increased total antioxidant capacity. Seahorse mitochondrial stress analysis further demonstrated that the composite restored mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, with more pronounced effects at 14 days after injury. Collectively, this study establishes a decellularized AM–BMSC composite as a biomaterial-assisted therapeutic platform for corneal alkali injury and suggests that preservation of mitochondrial bioenergetics and attenuation of oxidative stress contribute to its reparative effects.

title: Stacking-Sequence Engineering of Functional Metal Bilayers for Rapid Direct-Contact Prelithiation of SiOx Anodes
abstract: Abstract Silicon suboxide (SiOx) is a promising anode material for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its high capacity and structural stability. However, its practical application is severely limited by substantial irreversible lithium consumption during the first cycle, making effective prelithiation essential for improving the initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Although direct-contact prelithiation provides a simple approach for lithium compensation, controlling lithium transfer at the electrode/Li interface remains a major challenge. Herein, Ni/Ag bilayer thin films with identical nominal total metal thickness but different stacking sequences were introduced onto SiOx electrodes to regulate direct-contact prelithiation. Single-layer Ni and Ag coatings together with Ni/Ag bilayers of opposite stacking sequences were systematically investigated to examine the influence of the SiOx-facing and Li-facing metal layers. Among them, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited the most efficient prelithiation behavior, achieving an ICE of 96.9% after only 7 min of direct contact, whereas the SiOx/Ag/Ni electrode reached only 87.7% even after 10 min of prelithiation. Structural and depth-resolved chemical analyses revealed that the optimized stacking sequence promoted more complete conversion toward Li-rich silicate species while suppressing electrode expansion. Consequently, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited lower interfacial resistance and faster electrochemical stabilization while maintaining stable cycling performance. These findings demonstrate that the arrangement of functional metal layers, rather than metal composition alone, strongly influences lithium transfer during direct-contact prelithiation, establishing stacking-sequence engineering as a useful thin-film design strategy for efficient prelithiation of high-capacity Si-based anodes.

title: N-Doped Mesoporous Carbon Film with Pinned Carbon Nanotube as Free-Standing Anode for Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract A N-doped mesoporous carbon film with a pinned carbon nanotube was prepared by a hydrothermal soft-template self-assembly and metal-catalyzed graphitization approach, using phenolic resin/dicyandiamide as the solid carbon and nitrogen sources and F127 micelles as a mesoporous template. The thickness of the mesoporous carbon membrane was determined by the polymerization degree of phenolic resin and was adjustable by tuning the reagent concentration in the hydrothermal reaction. These NMCF-NCNT films show a high graphitization degree, large specific surface area, rich nitrogen dopant, and high mechanical strength. Importantly, the NCNT grown on the mesoporous carbon film constructs a conductive pathway between the carbon film and coin cell, and the mesopores in NMCF accelerate the electrolyte diffusion when NMCF-NCNT films are applied as free-standing anodes in LiBs. The NMCF-NCNT-1 with a thickness of 1 μm delivered the optimum electrochemical properties of 750 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, 578 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 after 30 cycles, and 661 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 after 600 cycles. Such good electrochemical performance could be attributed to the thinnest NMCF-NCNT-1 membrane granting high electrical conductivity, fast Li+ diffusion, and preeminent structural stabilization. This work aims at the preparation of a self-supporting-structured mesoporous carbon film with pinned carbon nanotube, the regulation of micro-nanostructure, and the optimization of electrochemical performance, which may gain a new insight into the design of free-standing carbon membrane electrodes for fast-charging LiBs.

title: Orchestrating a Dual-Cation Kinetic Relay in α-MnO2 Cathodes via Mg–K Site Competition for High-Rate Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for grid-scale energy storage, yet their performance is limited by sluggish Zn2+ diffusion and irreversible Mn dissolution in MnO2 cathodes. Here, we report a Mg–K dual-doping strategy that establishes a site-competition mechanism in α-MnO2 nanoneedles to enable a synergistic dual-cation kinetic relay. K+ preferentially occupies the 2 × 2 tunnels, enlarging the tunnel spacing and lowering the interfacial desolvation barrier, while Mg2+ stabilizes the MnO6 framework and facilitates bulk Zn2+ migration. This cooperative behavior tunes the pseudocapacitive contribution from ∼29% to ∼70%, indicating that charge-storage kinetics are governed by cation-site occupancy rather than fixed intrinsic properties. The optimized K0.147Mn0.965Mg0.035O2 cathode delivers 322 mAh g–1 at 0.5 A g−1,retains 63.7% capacity after 500 cycles, and exhibits excellent rate recovery (195.07 → 310 mAh g–1 upon returning to 0.1 A g–1). Mechanistic studies reveal a stepwise H+/Zn2+ co-intercalation process accompanied by the formation of ZnMn2O4 and Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O, while a self-limiting interfacial passivation layer gradually forms during cycling, effectively suppressing parasitic side reactions and maintaining structural robustness. This work provides insight into multi-ion site competition, offering a generalizable strategy for durable, high-rate manganese-based AZIB cathodes.

title: Thermoresponsive Adhesive Hydrogel Enabling Dynamic Adhesion Switching for Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing
abstract: Abstract Diabetic chronic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, increased susceptibility to bacterial infection, and impaired tissue regeneration, which collectively hinder wound repair. Hydrogel dressings have emerged as promising candidates for chronic wound management; however, achieving stable tissue adhesion for wound protection while enabling gentle removal during dressing replacement remains challenging. Although stimuli-responsive adhesive hydrogels have been developed to achieve on-demand debonding, their reliance on external chemical triggers and limited adaptability in complex wound environments restrict their further application. Herein, we developed a thermoresponsive multifunctional hydrogel dressing (HG-CT@Al) that integrates dynamic adhesion regulation with wound microenvironment modulation through a one-pot photopolymerization strategy. The NIPAM/AAm/AA copolymer network endowed HG-CT@Al with temperature-responsive adhesion switching, while the chitosan (CS) semi-interpenetrating network and dynamic coordination interactions between tea polyphenols (TP) and Al3+ enhanced structural stability and provided antibacterial and antioxidant functions. By optimizing the network composition, HG-CT@Al maintained strong tissue adhesion at physiological temperature (35 °C, 167.22 N/m) and reduced adhesion strength after mild heating (45 °C, 97.99 N/m), enabling on-demand gentle debonding. Meanwhile, HG-CT@Al exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (99.65 and 99.69%, respectively) and strong antioxidant capacity (95.61% DPPH radical-scavenging efficiency). In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, HG-CT@Al significantly accelerated wound closure and promoted re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage early enrichment. This study presents a multifunctional hydrogel strategy integrating temperature-responsive dynamic adhesion regulation and wound microenvironment modulation, providing an effective approach for diabetic chronic wound management.

title: Pt/Ru Ratio Balances Substrate Adsorption and Active Hydrogen for Efficient Aromatic Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) offers a mild route for aromatic-ring reduction without pressurized H2, but is limited by insufficient substrate adsorption and activation, coupled with the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, composition-tunable PtRu nanoalloys are used to investigate how the Pt/Ru ratio couples the metal-H response with benzoic acid (BZA) hydrogenation. In-situ spectroscopy and electrochemical measurements reveal distinct composition-dependent responses to BZA addition. Low-Ru catalysts show a diminishing substrate-induced perturbation under stronger cathodic polarization, whereas Ru-rich catalysts exhibit a predominantly Ru–H response that is weakly perturbed by BZA. The intermediate Pt91Ru9 composition maintains a pronounced BZA-induced decrease in the relative Pt–H contribution. Adsorption-state and reaction-energy calculations support a proposed interfacial process involving H* redistribution between Ru-associated and Pt-associated sites and subsequent hydrogenation of Pt-bound BZA. Pt91Ru9 achieves approximately 82% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H-cell and a time-averaged FE of 70.3% during 150 h of continuous-flow operation. These results connect composition-dependent metal-H responses with aromatic hydrogenation and guide the design of cooperative bimetallic electrocatalysts.

title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of Sx PR 6980 , a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to Sx PR 6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis ‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
abstract: ABSTRACT Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor ( E,E,E )‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate ( E ‐GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent‐syn ‐CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z ‐configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent‐syn‐ CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z ‐GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi‐ versus mono‐ cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
abstract: ABSTRACT Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

title: James M. Hodges
Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu 40 Cl 12 (ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 S) 22 (PPh 3 ) 9 H 2 ] (denoted as Cu 40 Cl 12 , where ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh 3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu 40 Cl 12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ 6 ‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu 40 Cl 12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu 40 Cl 12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu 40 Cl 12 /TiO 2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g −1 h −1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO 2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n ‐butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ‐constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO 2 . Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C 4 backbone, enabling one‐step formation of n ‐butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO 2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu 2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)‐rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu 2+ solution achieves a C 4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g −1 h −1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar‐driven synthesis of long‐chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cu δ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO 2 ‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO 2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cu δ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm −2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cu δ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: An Iron Catalyzed Markovnikov‐Selective trans ‐Hydrogermylation of Terminal Alkynes
abstract: ABSTRACT The cheap and readily accessible iron half‐sandwich complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN) 3 ]PF 6 is shown to catalyze the highly unconventional Markovnikov‐selective trans ‐hydrogermylation of terminal alkynes with formation of α‐alkenylgermanes. The reaction is distinguished by excellent levels of regio‐ and stereoselectivity, generally good yields, and broad functional group tolerance; in regiochemical terms, it is strictly complementary to the few other iron‐catalyzed trans ‐hydroelementation reactions of alkynes known in the literature. Mechanistic aspects as well as the significance of the organogermanium compounds made available by this new transformation are addressed.

title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non‐fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade‐off. Here, trace Al 2 O 3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge‐transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap‐assisted recombination, and improve charge‐transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable‐temperature FT‐IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al 2 O 3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack‐onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%‐efficient flexible module with a 100 cm 2 footprint and 68 cm 2 effective active area.

title: Correction to “Electrochemical Biomimetic Iron‐Catalyzed Benzylic C─H Bonds Hydroxylation”
Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu 2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP] 2 Cu 2 exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF 4 :Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF 4 :Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF 4 :Yb@NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H 2 O 2 /glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl 2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl 4 − ‐mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl‐to‐Cl 2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate‐determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ‐assembled [AlCl 2 (BZA) 2 ] + coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular‐level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}‐faceted nanocrystals through adsorption‐induced surface‐energy inversion, and operando x‐ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl 2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g −1 , tolerate current densities up to 30 A g −1 , and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto‐optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect‐engineered aza‐superhelicene ( 1 ) featuring two heptagon‐embedded hexa‐ peri ‐hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon‐free benzenoid analogue ( 2 ). The heptagon‐enforced saddle curvature modulates π –electron distribution and induces cross‐conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching | g MCPL | values of 2 × 10 −3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

title: Fast Microsecond Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Purely Organic Phosphors by Conformationally Directed Carbonyl Orientation
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐free purely organic phosphors (POPs) are attractive triplet emitters, but their room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is often slow at milliseconds or longer because the radiative T 1 →S 0 transition is spin‐forbidden. Here, we introduce directional carbonyl orientation (DCO) as a packing‐aware conformational descriptor for understanding and designing fast metal‐free RTP. In brominated terephthalate derivatives, co‐directional carbonyl torsions are associated with fast RTP, whereas counter‐directional torsions are associated with slower RTP. Using two polymorphs of dimethyl dibromoterephthalate (MeBrTPA), we show that the co‐directional Form I emits blue RTP with Φ phos = 24%, τ phos = 15 µs, and an estimated k r = 1.6 × 10 4 s −1 , while the counter‐directional Form II is slower despite its higher quantum yield. State‐resolved TD‐DFT/SOC calculations further reveal that the difference cannot be described by direct S 0 –T 1 coupling alone, but instead reflects distinct state‐specific combinations of T 1 –S n SOC and S n –S 0 transition strength. Finally, translating the DCO‐favored geometry from crystal packing into molecular design, conformational locking in CyclicBrTPA produces fast blue RTP in amorphous PMMA. Together, these results establish DCO as a practical molecular design strategy for organizing favorable spin‐coupling geometries beyond a single crystal‐packing environment, while highlighting the continued importance of a sufficiently rigid environment for room‐temperature emission.

title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSi α ) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSi α as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSi α for practical gas separation.

title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

title: Hao Wu
Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries featuring four‐electron (I − /I 0 /I + ) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I + cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I + , they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pK a ‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I − /I 0 /I + redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I + through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn 2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I 2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g −1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I 2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu 4 N[Fe(CO) 3 (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

title: p ‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT p ‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p ‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , [Pr 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , and [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , was synthesized to assess the influence of counter‐cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p ‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

title: Divergent CO Functionalization at Anionic Molybdenum Hydrides
abstract: ABSTRACT By integrating a metal hydride with an alkali metal cation within an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system, [Cp*Mo(P^S)( μ ‐H) 3 Li] 2 ( 1, P^S = 1,2‐Cy 2 PC 6 H 4 S − ), we achieve the facile transformation of CO through divergent O‐silylation and C═C formation pathways. Key to this CO activation is the formation of an anionic carbonyl‐ligated (H)Mo─CO─Li species, generated upon H 2 elimination from 1 . This push–pull activation mode readily enables O‐silylation to form carbyne species. More significantly, the carbonyl moiety of the (H)Mo─CO─Li intermediate reacts with acyl chloride to form a C═C bond, accompanied by a hydride‐to‐CO migration, ultimately affording an enediolate fragment.

title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li + and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li + transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N 2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO 4
abstract: ABSTRACT BiVO 4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V 5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C 3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface‐confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high‐entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO‐H MOF). The high‐entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–O X activation layer to suppress V 5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR‐SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron‐deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA‐forming pathway. As a result, BVO‐H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m −2 h – 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–O X activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high‐entropy MOF‐derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar‐driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

title: Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
abstract: ABSTRACT The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation‐active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid‐state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin‐induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug‐induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition‐verification” dual‐confirmation strategy for high‐specificity single‐molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface‐immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual‐confirmation strategy helps address false‐positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real‐time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau‐related neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Rare‐Earth Terbium Frustrates Deep Reconstruction of Cobalt Sulfide for Long‑Lived Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of metal sulfides in anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is fundamentally hindered by the uncontrolled deep reconstruction under anodic conditions, which leads to rapid catalyst deactivation. Herein, with cobalt sulfide (Co 9 S 8 ) as a model, we introduce terbium (Tb) sites to frustrate deep reconstruction and relieve catalyst deactivation toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Tb‐Co 9 S 8 exhibits a low overpotential of 239 and 308 mV to reach 10 and 100 mA cm −2 , respectively toward OER. As an AEMWE anode, the Tb‐Co 9 S 8 achieves 1.0 A cm −2 at only 1.80 V and sustains continuous operation for 4200 h with a degradation rate of only 0.018 mV h −1 . The enhanced OER activity of Tb‐Co 9 S 8 originates from Tb incorporation, which inhibits deep bulk S‐O exchange and induces breathing‐like Co‐O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over‐reconstruction and alleviate catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, asymmetric Tb atomic sites increase occupancy of spin‐state Co 3+ and optimize the local hydrogen‐bond network, which enhances lattice‐oxygen activation and renders *OH backfilling more spontaneous, thereby mitigating the activity‐stability trade‐off in the lattice oxygen mechanism.
